articleTitle: Design of wearable textile antenna with various substrate and investigation on fabric selection
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In field of wearable technology one challenging improvement is wearable textile antenna. Primary requirement for wearable textile antennas are flexible construction materials which includes fabric with planar structure. Properties of the textile antenna such as bandwidth, efficiency, input impedance etc. depend upon type of substrate materials used. These properties are mostly determined by the substrate dielectric constant. Fabric material dielectric constant accurate value is to be calculated from resonant frequency of patch antenna. In this paper, rectangular microstrip patch antenna with different materials like cotton, polyester, lycra, cordura with different dielectric properties is design mathematically and simulated using IE3D software. Its influences on antenna parameters are investigated for designing of textile antenna with good efficiency.

articleTitle: An all-optical ultra-compact 4-channel wavelength de-multiplexer
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Design of an ultra-compact all optical 4 channel de-multiplexer is proposed in this work based on a two dimensional photonic crystal (PhC) structure. The PhC is formed using some silicon rods suspended in the air medium, which are arranged in a square lattice in a footprint of 75.24 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed component is designed to de-multiplex the wavelengths 1.31 μm, 1.43 μm, 1.55 μm and 1.7 μm. Simulations are performed using the Plane Wave Expansion (PWE) and the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) methods which exhibit that the device offers a high contrast ratio ~ 49 dB and a high data rate ~ 3.8 Tbit/s.

articleTitle: A compact printed UWB monopole antenna with triple band notch characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this communication a compact printed microstrip-fed triple band-notched Ultra Wideband (UWB) antenna is presented. Notch bands encompassing 3.3–3.8 GHz Wi-MAX, 5.15–5.85 GHz WLAN and 7.9–8.4 GHz X-band satellite communication link are achieved by etching a Hilbert slot on the radiating monopole, etching a modified rectangular defect on the ground structure and the application of a fractal resonator respectively. The antenna's Ultra wide bandwidth ranges from 2.6 GHz to 12 GHz (VSWR ≤ 2). The agreement between the simulation and empirical results advocates that the intended antenna can be a worthy candidate for various UWB communication systems.

articleTitle: An enhanced beam scanning leaky-wave antenna with suppressed open-stop band
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a rectangular substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) leaky-wave antenna. This antenna support continuous backward to forward scanning. The antenna consists of longitudinal slots along with inductive posts. The longitudinal slot has been used for backward to forward radiation of space harmonic -1 with open-stopband (OSB) because of impedance mismatched in OSB. By introducing additional inductive post that resolves the problem of impedance mismatched, hence OSB is suppressed. The proposed antenna is designed for 10-16 GHz with scanning angle from -55° through broadsides to 34°.

articleTitle: Detection of N, P, K fertilizers in agricultural soil with NIR laser absorption technique
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Soil is a complex medium that contains minerals, organic matter, micro-organisms, air and water. Recent studies have shown that soil fertility is declining in many farmlands due to insufficient fertilization. Over-fertilization results in groundwater pollution or toxic accumulation of chemicals in the soil. The aim of this experiment is to adjust fertilization based on crop needs and soil properties and to reduce the amount of fertilizer in soil without diminishing yield. The soil analysis technique focus on photon absorption characteristics of the major soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium). The soil samples under test were first oven dried and and then mixed with four types of fertilizer [KNO3, TSP, (NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>, NPK] in the concentration range of 0.02-10%. Near IR laser beam pass through the closed loop Mach-Zander Interferometer to reduce fluctuations related to beam path and interacts with soil sample. When IR radiations are focused onto a sample, the molecules in the sample will increase their vibration energy by absorbing energy at specific frequencies depending on the molecular geometry, bond strengths and atomic masses. The scattered beam is thus modified, creating a signature of the targeted object with peaks at the absorbing frequencies. This technique provided rapid, non-destructive and simultaneous determination of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium concentrations in soil fertilizer mixtures.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator based circularly polarized MIMO antenna for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A dual-port dielectric resonator (DR) based circularly polarized multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna is reported for wireless local area network (WLAN) applications. In this antenna, a corner truncated V-shaped DR is used to obtain circular polarization (CP) radiation. Along with this, two symmetric orthogonal feed networks are deployed to lessen mutual coupling between the ports. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that the reported MIMO antenna has a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 10.28% (4.89-5.42 GHz) and a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 4.17% (5.16-5.38 GHz). Also, diversity performance of proposed MIMO antenna is evaluated by using envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG).

articleTitle: A dual wideband monopole antenna for GSM/UMTS/LTE/WiFi/and lower UWB application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper a dual wideband monopole antenna is proposed for various wireless applications such as GSM, UMTS, LTE, WiFi, WiMax and lower UWB application. It is designed using two sickle shaped parallel radiator patch, feed by single microstrip feed line, defected ground plane, and rectangular slot in ground plane. The simulation and measured result shows that it has impedance bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; - 10) of 60.46% over (1.5-2.8 GHz) and 60.86% over (3.2-6 GHz). The proposed antenna design has gain between 1.0 to 4.0 dBi. It is designed using low cost lossy FR4 substrate with relative permittivity of 4.3 and it has compact volume of 57×37.5×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The result and design makes the proposed antenna suitable for mobile/wireless and lower UWB applications.

articleTitle: A compact 4-port UWB-MIMO/diversity antenna for WPAN application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact 4-port ultrawideband (UWB) MIMO/diversity antenna with low ECC is presented. The design employ frequently used orthogonal orientation to achieve high isolation within a chip space of 42×42 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna parameter such as the impedance bandwidth, isolation, 3-D radiation pattern, peak gain, radiation efficiency have been studied. Moreover, diversity performance in terms of envelop correlation coefficient (ECC) from far field pattern has been analyzed.

articleTitle: A wideband 1:2 T-junction power divider for antenna array with optimum results
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a symmetrical T-junction power divider has been proposed for 2.45 GHz application. This is used to split the total incident power equally by using quarter wave transformer, stepped impedance transformer and mitered corners. It is a generalized wideband power divider with optimum reflection and transmission characteristics and VSWR of 1.006, simulated using a commercial electromagnetic 3-D simulator CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: A compact microstrip patch antenna with five circular slots for wideband applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Design of a compact microstrip patch antenna with five circular slots for wideband applications is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is printed on both sides of a single substrate. On one side of square substrate, first a square patch is printed and then five circular slots are etched. On the other side of the substrate, a rectangular microstrip line is printed to feed the antenna. The antenna is simulated using high frequency structure simulation (HFSS) software and the optimal location and dimension of the slots and feed element are obtained. Further, the proposed antenna is fabricated on a glass epoxy FR-4 substrate. The proposed antenna has a wideband from 1.91GHz to 6.19 GHz with four resonant frequencies of 2.05 GHz, 2.86 GHz, 3.49 GHz and 5.11 GHz. The simulated and measured results are compared and these are in good agreement. The antenna can be used for wideband applications in frequency range from 1.91GHz to 6.19 GHz.

articleTitle: Design methodologies for survivable elastic optical networks with guardband-constrained spectral allocation
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper presents design methodologies for elastic optical networks (EONs) with due considerations to the survivability against link failures and guardband-constrained spectral allocations, using ILP and heuristic algorithms. The obtained results show that, there should be a tradeoff between the number of guardband slots and the spectrum utilization in EONs. Further, a comparative study has been carried out for blocking probabilities of general (unprotected) and survivable EONs with two different protection mechanisms, with due consideration to guardband slots.

articleTitle: Investigation of optimum position of interface between strip waveguide and PhC Slot waveguide for maximum power coupling
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article investigates the suitable interface to attain the highest transmittance for a butt coupling of a strip and slotted photonic crystal waveguide. Different interfaces have been studied and it has been found that an interface position has a significant role in the coupling. Width of the strip waveguide has been varied to observe its effect in the transmittance. The result shows that a particular interface, denoted here as CC' found to be offering the best butt coupling for these waveguides, irrespective of the width of strip.

articleTitle: A compact modified star shape microstrip patch antenna for wideband application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Design and radiation performance of a compact modified star shaped microstrip patch antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is printed on both sides of a single substrate. On one side of substrate, first a square patch is printed and then one star shaped slot and six circular slots are etched. On the other side of the substrate, a rectangular microstrip line is printed to feed the antenna. The antenna is simulated using high frequency structure simulation (HFSS) software. The proposed antenna has a wideband characterstics from 2.166 GHz to 4.245 GHz with impedance bandwidth of 64.9%. The simulated and measured results are compared and these are in good agreement. The antenna can be used for wideband applications in frequency range from 2.166 GHz to 4.245 GHz.

articleTitle: A dual band wearable metamaterial absorber with reduced cross-polarized reflection
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article presents a dual band metamaterial absorber on a flexible substrate material for wearable applications in the microwave frequency. The substrate material chosen is felt whose dielectric constant is 1.2, loss tangent of 0.02 and thickness is 1mm. The dual band absorption is obtained at 6.18 GHz and 10.77 GHz respectively. An array of cross dipole metallic patch layer is placed at the middle of the substrate layer to reduce the cross polarization reflection as a consequence relative absorption bandwidth (RAB) of 39.53% is enhanced at 10.77 GHz.

articleTitle: Motion detection and tracking using microwave sensor for eliminating illegal mine activities
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a X-band microwave motion sensor is utilized to accurately detect any object in motion and the interfacing circuit of microwave motion sensor with the microcontroller is been proposed. The unauthorized areas of mines are kept under investigation using a wireless sensor network (WSN) formed by microwave motion sensor nodes, each node is kept at a distance of 20 meters from one another. The sensor node consists of microwave motion sensor, a microcontroller and a Wi-Fi module. The paper elaborates the unique characteristics of microwave motion sensor that makes it ideal for eradicating illegal activities in mines with the help of the concept “Internet of Things”. The paper also explains the effectiveness of the proposed amplifier circuit using simulation results in LTSpice IV 180nm technology for practical use.

articleTitle: Spaceborne bistatic polarimetrie SAR for scattering analysis and classification of man-made and natural features
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Polarimetrie Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR), is an emerging technology in the field of remote sensing today which has several applications in a number of study areas. It has a unique feature as it combines the enhanced resolution that is available through the use of SAR with the wave properties of Polarised electromagnetic energy caused due to scattering of radiation as it interacts with different features on earth's surface. A polarimetric backscatter signature is a three-dimensional saddle plot which is created when ellipticity, orientation angle and amplitude of the backscattered polarised wave is graphed. Since different features interact differently with the polarised wave, each man-made and natural feature causes a unique scattering of the polarised wave which is studied in the backscatter signature received. Based on different scattering mechanisms, a number of decomposition models were proposed like Freeman's decomposition model, Sinclair decomposition model, Pauli's decomposition, Yamaguchi's decomposition model and many more. Based on the relative scattering of the polarised wave, the identification and classification of various feature classes was possible. In this study it was aimed to study the different polarimetric decomposition models and the man-made and natural features detected in each, based on the relative scattering mechanisms and their relative classification using machine learning and object oriented approaches with improved classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of dual-band dual-directional metamaterial absorber for space application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A Novel Dual-Band and Dual-Directional Metamaterial Absorber (DBDDMA) is proposed. Here we have introduced a new of its kind of absorber which will absorb EM wave in asymmetric propagation direction with two absorption bands in both direction. Simulation result shows that it has two absorption peaks with 90% and 85% absorption in one direction and has two absorption peaks of 91% and 83% in another direction.

articleTitle: Novel design of multi band compact planar RF sensor for liquid testing
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel design topology of Planar RF sensor using the three S-CSRRs (single ring-complementary split ring resonators) is presented. To achieve the compact design of triple band sensor, orientation of all the three rings are kept same. Numerical simulation and optimization of the proposed sensor is carried out using the CST-MWS in order to tune the resonance frequencies of the S-CSRRs at the frequency range of interest viz., ISM band (1.8GHz, 2.45 GHz) and Wi-Fi band (3.5GHz). Finally, the fabricated prototype of designed sensor is developed and sensitivity analysis is performed by measuring the dielectric samples having similar value of dielectric constant. Afterward, adulteration detection of edible oils is performed to show the applicability of proposed sensor.

articleTitle: Phase characterization of a liquid crystal spatial light modulator
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Liquid crystal spatial light modulator is a versatile device to be used in different areas of modern optical studies. The traditional Twyman-Green interferometer is used to measure phase modulation characteristics of PLUTO phase-only spatial light modulator produced by Holoeye Company. Earlier fringe shift used to be measured manually due to which there is always some possibility of inaccuracy created by human intervention. We propose improved method to process interference fringes and measure shift distance by computer to avoid human error.

articleTitle: An optimization technique utilizing genetic algorithm for the synthesis of large thinned planar antenna array with low peak side lobe level
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient optimization technique for the synthesis of large thinned planar antenna (LTPA) arrays is proposed. The main objective is to achieve optimal planar thinned array configuration which yields lowest possible low peak side lobe levels (PSLL). Towards this aim, authors employed improved genetic algorithm (IGA) in which some advancement in crossover and mutation operators are introduced to enhance algorithm performance. A 50×50-element LTPA array is numerically analysed to assess the performance of the proposed method. Results obtained through this study demonstrate that significant amount of reduction in PSLL is acheived.

articleTitle: A broadband hybrid GaN cascode low noise amplifier for WiMax applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a 3.5 GHz GaN Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) using Microstrip interconnect technology on a gold plated PCB and using packaged commercial GaN-on-SiC HEMTs. Cascode configuration with inter-stage matching and independent biasing networks was used. The whole design was fully implemented using Microstrip except for the capacitors and was optimized to reduce the noise figure (NF) and improve the gain and stability. The LNA provided a gain of 13.5 dB with a noise figure (NF) less than 3dB from 2.9 to 3.7 GHz with power consumption 2.92W.

articleTitle: Dual band circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna for X-band applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A dual band Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna (CPDRA) is presented in this paper. A single feed, aperture coupling technique is being used to obtain the CPDRA. A cross shaped DRA is placed above a rectangular ring-shaped slot which is truncated at the four corners. The slot is fed by a 50Ω microstrip line present on the opposite side. The proposed design gives a Fractional Bandwidth of 15% and 4.4% and 3-dB Axial Ratio Bandwidth 0.2 & 0.17 GHz around 8.0 and 11.2 GHz, respectively. The maximum gains at both the bands are 6.1 and 4.4 dBic, respectively. A detailed analysis of the operating principle and the results of the prototype are being carried out in this paper.

articleTitle: Modelling of CZTS/ZnS/AZO solar cell for efficiency enhancement
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, we report on improvement of solar efficiency which uses CZTS as active absorber, CdS as buffer layer and AZO (Al doped ZnO) as window layer. All the material layers have modeled using the optical constants and the model were validated better agreement with experimental results. The performances of solar cells with ZnS material instead of CdS buffer for the development of more environmentally friendly devices have been studied. CZTS solar cell with ZnS as buffer layer shows improved performance owing to its higher band gap and less absorption compared to CdS buffer thereby promoting more photons to the active absorber layer. Hence the efficiency of the device has risen from 8.49% to 9.16%.

articleTitle: A 4×4 slot MIMO antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A printed four element MIMO antenna constitutes with 2 slot elements as a common radiator is proposed in this paper. Individual slot element is fed by a pair of microstrip fed lines. Two different pairs of defected ground structure (DGS) are etched over the slot elements to enhance the isolation between the four ports. The 10 dB return loss bandwidth of the antenna covers 5.6-6.36GHz. The gain of the prototype is 3.95dB. Essential matrices like TARC, ECC and DG are also evaluated to realize the diversity performance.

articleTitle: Dual broadband high gain SIW slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel design of dual broadband high gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity backed slot array antenna is described. The SIW cavity is design in dominant mode TE10. The proposed antenna is design by two pair of λg/2-resonators cavity backed slot on broad wall of single layer substrate integrated waveguide. To place two pair unequal slot length in stair nature on broad-wall of SIW cavity are responsible to broadening the bandwidth at two different frequency band and also due to arraying nature of slot enhanced the gain. The proposed antenna have Lower frequency bandwidth 4.4% (9.58 GHz-10.02 GHz) and higher frequency bandwidth is 9.49% (10.84 GHz-11.92 GHz) with 10 dB gain at lower band and 9.4 dB gain at higher band. The proposed antenna has high gain, directive radiation field with high FTBR.

articleTitle: 30-Gb/s low power inductorless CMOS transimpedance amplifier for optical receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A 30Gb/s inductorless CMOS transimpedance amplifier (TIA) for optical communication receiver is presented in 0.18-μm CMOS technology. The TIA incorporates three stages of differential amplifiers with an active negative feedback. The feedback network provides a bandwidth of 7GHz in addition to the bandwidth offered by the three stages of the differential amplifier. The proposed inductorless TIA achieves a transimpedance gain of 45dB with 3dB bandwidth of 21.23GHz. The design has input referred noise current density of 63.1 pA/√Hz and jitter of 9.07 ps. The power consumption of the TIA is 10.296mW with a supply voltage of 1.8 V.

articleTitle: CPW fed slot dipole antenna with comb shape for satellite applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Today, there is a great change in wireless technology due to which there is an increase in demand of hand held devices. More the technology updates, a more need for miniaturized antenna with better efficiency and bandwidth can be observed. A Coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed antenna with comb shaped structure for satellite communication is proposed. The antenna presented here has dimensions of 101mm × 36.6mm. The antenna is to be fabricated on 0.5cm of top surface of RT/Duroid substrate with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=2.2 & tanδ=0.0009. Simulation results are to be performed using IE3D simulator. The antenna has peak resonance at 4GHz frequency which makes it suitable. The fractional bandwidth of an antenna shows 1.5%. The antenna achieves peak gain of 10 dBi.

articleTitle: Estimating root zone soil moisture from AMSR2 remotely sensed surface soil moisture data
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Significance of root zone soil moisture can be observed in agricultural practices and meteorological phenomenon and estimation of the same become vital. There is always a correlation between surface and root zone soil moisture and thus a relationship between satellite soil moisture, ground measured soil moisture and modelled soil moisture is investigated here. An R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of ~0.5 and ~0.73 is noted between the Soil Water Index (SWI), derived from AMSR2 data, ground data and GLDAS-NOAH modelled soil moisture data. The analysis is performed for IIT Kanpur for the year 2013.

articleTitle: A flexible corrugated vivaldi antenna for radar and see-through wall applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A Tapered Slot Flexible Corrugated Vivaldi (FCV) antenna has been designed for the radar and see-through wall applications, using CST Microwave Studio. It has been designed over a flexible polyimide substrate, having thickness 0.25mm, by depositing 0.01mm silver film. Corrugations with constant width and spacing, with a constant decreasing rate are cut throughout the exponential section. Also, silver metal strips are being employed periodically over the substrate. In the spacing between the grating elements, the circular silver metal portions are applied so as to further enhance the antenna performance. The parameters of the antenna are optimized so as to get an efficient antenna.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband down-conversion mixer in X-band
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband single balanced down-conversion diode based passive mixer is presented. RF bandwidth of this single balanced mixer is made wider with the help of two section BLC and double stub matching. The mixer has high RF sensitivity up to −90 dBm. The mixer down-converts the RF band 9.2–10.5 GHz to 1.3–2.6 GHz. A prototype is fabricated and tested. It provides measured average conversion loss of 10 dB over the entire RF bandwidth at an optimum LO power of 13 dBm with measured IP1 of −1.6 dBm. Over the band, RF-LO isolation is at least 30 dB.

articleTitle: Soil moisture detection using CSRR based submersible RF sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work a novel design of CSRR loaded submersible planar RF sensor is presented. The proposed sensor has a quite high sensitivity as compared to the other reported planar RF sensors. Design and optimization of proposed sensor is performed using the CST-MWS. Finally the designed sensor is fabricated on the 0.8 mm Roger 5880 substrate. Proposed work can be appreciated in term of its applicability for very small percentage moisture detection in the different variant of available soil/sand samples.

articleTitle: FBG based sensing architecture for traffic surveillance in railways
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In recent years, derailment of train is one of the major concern of Indian railways. This could be hazardous and may cost lives of passengers. To avoid such situations, a new optical sensing architecture is being proposed in this paper, which utilizes Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) as optical sensor. Through this architecture train speed, location of the train and damage point location can be estimated by the base station.

articleTitle: Compact four-element 8-shaped self-affine fractal UWB MIMO antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A compact four-element 8-shaped self-affine fractal UWB MIMO antenna is presented. The self-affine fractal structure provides miniaturization and wideband characteristics to the antenna. The 8-shaped self-affine fractal geometry is designed up to the second iteration by iterated function system (IFS). This reduces the single-element antenna area by 24.88%. The dimension of proposed compact MIMO antenna is 44×44 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and its impedance bandwidth ranges (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB) from 3.1 GHz to 11 GHz. The mutual coupling is lesser than -16 dB across the entire operating frequency band. The correlation coefficient is less than 0.1 and diversity gain is more than 9.95 across the operating frequency band. Results of this antenna indicate that it is suitable for UWB applications.

articleTitle: An ultra wideband microstrip bandpass filter with wide stopband using SIR and DGS
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper an ultra wideband microstrip Bandpass filter is proposed using stepped impedance resonators (SIR) and defected ground structures (DGS). This band-pass filter is designed to operate within the Ultra Wide Band frequency range from 4.0 GHz to 11.0 GHz with 7.0 GHZ bandwidth and centre frequency at 7.5 GHz. This prototype filter is designed on RT/Duroid 5880 substrate of thickness 0.787mm with dielectric constant 2.2. The filter is simulated and optimized using Zealand IE3D simulation software v14.0. The passband of the filter has five transmission poles. Insertion loss within the passband is better than -1.5dB and the return loss is kept less than -20dB and a total fractional bandwidth of 93.33% is obtained. The prototype built can be used in UWB communications or localization systems.

articleTitle: FBG sensing system to study the bridge weigh-in-motion for measuring the vehicle parameters
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, an FBG based Weigh-in-Motion (WIM) sensing system is designed by using two FBGs, each one attached at the central span portion of the girder between two piers of a bridge model. The FBG's are pasted at an inclination of 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. Experiments were conducted to study the response of the designed WIM system varying the loads and velocity of the vehicle. The temporal response of the FBG's and shift in the wavelength is recorded using interrogator of resolution 1pm. The response of the sensor system for velocity and load showed a linear variation with a good correlation up to 150m/sec velocity and 5N weight respectively. The results reveal that the proposed system is capable of monitoring the dynamic response due to the changes in the load and velocity of the moving vehicle over the bridge.

articleTitle: A 2.45 GHz harmonic suppression array antenna for rectenna application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 2.45 GHz harmonic suppression capability of array antenna has been presented for wireless power transfer applications. Harmonic suppression up to a fourth order of the fundamental operating frequency has been achieved by using rectangular slot Defected Ground Structure (DGS). The designed antenna uses an FR4 material having thickness 1.6 mm as a substrate which has loss tangent tan(δ) 0.02. The gain and radiation efficiency are 4.5dB, 75% respectively. This antenna is suitable for rectenna applications.

articleTitle: Design of a high performance bias tee and its application to a switchable true time delay line
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A high performance bias tee is designed in microstrip line technology. It is shown that a single capacitor and a section of high impedance line are enough to achieve an RF isolation of at least 30 dB over 40% bandwidth. The bias tee is used to implement a switchable true time delay (TTD) line over 2–3 GHz frequency band with a delay difference variation less than 0.025 ns.

articleTitle: Negative refractive index metamaterial for enhancing radiation directivity in S-band
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A new design of metamaterial having a negative refractive index in the whole of S-band (2.2-3.3 GHz) is shown which resonates at 2.5 GHz with less than -40 dB of the reflection coefficient, thus showing a perfect transmission. The radiation pattern with and without metamaterial is compared. It is seen that the radiation directivity is enhanced due to the metamaterial when the half power beamwidth is compared. This structure can be used in the application like wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Compact antenna based on SRR using radial stub as virtual ground for wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper presents the design of a miniaturized antenna which consist of Split Ring Resonator (SRR) and radial stub as virtual ground. The proposed antenna has a physical size of 0.16 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.27 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.013 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with a gain of 1.81 dBi in the operating frequency range. The antenna shows 8.7% impedance bandwidth at 2.42 GHz and radiation efficiency of 93%, making it suitable for use in wireless applications.

articleTitle: Performance enhancement of a novel 2-D code based atmospheric OCDMA system
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, performance enhancement of one-coincidence frequency hopping code/quadratic congruence code (OCFHC/QCC) based two-dimensional (2-D) optical code division multiple access (OCDMA) system is studied using Reed-Solomon (R-S) code in presence of multiple user interference (MUI) and turbulence. Atmospheric turbulence is presumed to be weak and follows lognormal distribution. For OCFHC/QCC code, probability density function of interference is trinomial. It is observed that error probability improves by an order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> with R-S code for four simultaneous users and alternatively transmitted power requirement decreases.

articleTitle: Triple band dual polarized planar slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A multiband planar antenna fed by coplanar waveguide technique is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is a microstrip slot antenna having CPW feed with circular and linear polarization characteristics. The proposed antenna is a 40×40mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> structure designed on FR4 substrate of thickness 1.6mm on CST Microwave Studio. Designed antenna resonates at 2.4GHz, 4.62GHz and 7.0GHz which can be used for bluetooth, radio navigation, satellite communication and radiolocation applications. The lower and upper bands are circular polarized while the mid band is linearly polarized.

articleTitle: An expeditious synthesis of thinned planar antenna array by exploitation of multi-objective optimization technique
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-objective optimization technique to synthesize uniformly excited thinned planar antenna (UE-TPA) array with optimum peak side lobe level (PSLL), better average side lobe level (ASLL), narrowest possible half power beam width (HPBW) and higher directivity or gain. A modified binary coded genetic algorithm (MBC-GA) is employed to determine the best suitable combination of `ON' and `OFF' elements in an UE-TPA array corresponding to ameliorated aforesaid design parameters. To corroborate the capability of proposed method, a 10×20-element UE-TPA array is numerically analysed. Results obtained through the proposed approach are compared with those of previously published which shows that present method outmatches the methods available in literature.

Author Keywords: uniformly excited thinned planar antenna (UE-TPA) array

articleTitle: Compact metamaterial inspired dual-band bandpass filter using parallel coupled line and circular shaped stub
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metamaterial inspired dual-band bandpass filter. The filter discussed is constructed using two parallel-coupled lines, interconnected with two circular shaped stubs. The designed filter offers a 3 dB fractional bandwidth of 70.6% and 26.2% with centre frequencies of 1.77 GHz and 4.13 GHz for first and second pass band. Both the pass bands are separated by a stop band of 1.2 GHz. This filter offers compactness with electrical size of 0.10λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, given λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is wavelength in free space at centre frequency of first passband. The average group delay for both the pass bands are 0.4 ns and 0.6 ns respectively. The modeling of proposed filter is carried out by high frequency structural simulator ANSYS HFSS 14.0 3D software. It is useful in global systems for mobile communications (GSM) at 1800 MHz and fixed satellite service (3.7–4.2 GHz).

articleTitle: Size dependent triboelectric nanogenerator and effect of temperature
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A layered structure of triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) has been fabricated in the contact separation mode with plain paper, highly dielectric (PTFE) polytetrafluoroethylene and conductive aluminium layers, respectively. The output responses were recorded in form of electrical voltage by the triggering of mechanical interactions over the TENGs surface. A size dependent analysis has been studied, followed by the function of current density and generated power. Thermal behaviour on the TENG surface revealed an inverse output voltage response.

articleTitle: High efficiency low power series diode rectifier design
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the multisection impedance matching design on Series diode rectifier at 2.45 GHz using Advanced Design System (ADS) software. This rectifier is used for applications involving RF to DC rectification for low input power sources. Input matching circuit has been optimized for high efficiency. Simulated results show that 62% and 52% RF to DC conversion efficiency have been achieved for input power 0 dBm and -5 dBm respectively at 2.45GHz. A peak efficiency of 85% is simulated for an input power of 18 dBm and a 3.2V output DC voltage is achieved at a 1KΩ DC load when the rectifier is matched to 50Ω.

articleTitle: A high isolation MIMO cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna for 4G applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article, cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) based multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna system has been investigated for 4G applications. Isolation of proposed antenna has been improved by generation orthogonal modes in CDR. The fractional impedance bandwidth for port-1 and port-2 is 11.9% and 10.6% respectively and within the operating band, the proposed radiator achieves a high isolation (S12) of greater than -25dB. Different MIMO performance parameters (ECC, DG and CCL) are also calculated and found within the acceptable limit.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of microstrip slot antenna using SRR and CSRR loading
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The design of a miniaturized slot antenna based on SRR and CSRR loading is presented. The SRR and CSRR were properly placed to get excited by the electromagnetic fields of the slot antenna. The miniaturization was done with out increasing lateral or longitudinal dimensions of the existing antenna. A miniaturization of approximately 22% is achieved. The radiation characteristics of the miniaturized antenna are almost similar to that of the unloaded slot with low cross polarization levels. The resonance frequency of slot antenna was brought down from 4.2 GHz to 3.3 GHz with loading. The simulations were carried out using the ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: Reflection-type dispersive delay line using stepped impedance stub
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, it is shown that a stepped-impedance open-stub can be used to design a reflection type dispersive delay line with peak delays more than tens of nano seconds. A loss less transmission line model is used for analysis. Finally, a delay line is fabricated that provides a measured delay of 22.23 ns at 2.5 GHz. Total rectangular area of the unit is 60 mm × 40 mm on a 0.5 mm thick substrate with dielectric constant 3.55.

articleTitle: Analysis of offset reflector performance fed by 2×2 microstrip antenna array using GO technique
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper investigates an offset reflector antenna system performance for a 2×2 microstrip planar array feed. Here, the cross-polar and sidelobe levels for an offset reflector antenna operating in the Ka-band frequency of 20 GHz are evaluated for variation in separation between array elements placed at the focal plane of the parabolic reflector. The antenna array is designed to illuminate an offset reflector antenna having a diameter D = 50λ and F/D ratio 0.6, Fis focal length. The simulation studies have been carried out using HFSS 15.0 to verify the analytical results obtained using GO.

articleTitle: Categorization of concealed radioactive waste for microwave treatment
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In the nuclear industry, various microwave or conventional heating techniques are being utilized for processing of radioactive waste in order to reduce its hazardous effects to facilitate the safe disposal. In this paper, the microwave treatment of radioactive waste is explored by estimating the dielectric properties of various nuclear gradable materials such as concretes concealed in a non-metallic container using the time domain technique. The main focus here is to monitor the changes in the dielectric properties along with the loss factor of investigating media which can be useful in order to process the radioactive waste materials concealed in the non-metallic container.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband unidirectional antenna for microwave head imaging system
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Head imaging system requires the antenna with low profile structure having directional radiation pattern and lower operating frequency range. The essential features like wide bandwidth, reduced dimension, and unidirectional radiation characterize the microwave imaging (MI) systems for biomedical applications. The article reports the design of a compact microstrip antenna and analysis with an operating frequency from 2.46 GHz-3.30 GHz. The lower frequency range satisfies the requirement of proper signal penetration into the human head. The antenna provides the radiation efficiency more than 84%. The proposed design covers 29.16% of fractional bandwidth with considerable radiation characteristics. The dimension of the designed antenna is 0. 58λ × 0.49λ × 0.12 λ, where λ represents the wavelength of the smallest frequency in the required band of operation. This antenna shows stable gain and good radiation efficiency that can be used for biomedical applications in microwave imaging (MI) systems.

articleTitle: Design and performance analysis of MMI based all optical logic gates on SOI substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We propose MMI based all optical logic gates which are used for various logic functions. The input signal is considered as logical `0' or `1' according to phase of the signal and the output of a device is depend upon the intensity of light i.e. low intensity means `0' and high intensity means `1'. Hence the propose device is used to convert input phase information to amplitude information at the output port. The proposed MMI structure has ultracompact dimension of 2.5 μm × 10.6 μm that can be used in Photonics integrated circuits. We have used Beam propagation method to analyze the performance of the device. Simulation results show that the ON-OFF extinction ratio of OR, NAND, XOR, XNOR, and NOT optical logic gates are 18.5, 18.5, 20.1, 20.1 and 20.1 dB respectively in whole C-band.

articleTitle: On-chip nanophotonic devices for optical communication and interconnects
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: On-chip nanophotonic devices are promising for next-generation communication systems and data centres which require guiding and controlling light at nano scales. Some nanophotonic devices with engineered and/or hybrid materials are proposed. A nanophotonic coupler with ultra-short coupling length of 0.461-μm is proposed. Also, photonic crystals based devices for delay tuning and for on-chip biosensing are proposed.

articleTitle: Compact two-element cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna array for quad-band applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article, the simulation and experimental analysis of compact two-element cylindrical dielectric resonant antenna (CDRA) array for quad-band application. C-shaped microstrip feed is utilised to excite the two cylindrical dielectric resonators. Combination of wide bandwidth and high gain is always a challenge for researchers. The proposed antenna array shows quad-band characteristics i.e. 2.18–3.3 GHz, 5.5–8.2 GHz, 9.48–12.6 GHz, and 14.3–16.1 GHz with the fractional bandwidth of 40.8%, 19.7%, 27.48% and 11.84 % respectively. The fractional bandwidths are calculated with respect to the central frequency. The parametric analysis, impedance bandwidth and radiation characteristics of proposed antenna have been extracted with the help of Ansoft HFSS simulation software. The prototype of antenna is fabricated to validate the simulated results. The proposed antenna array affords compact size, appropriate gain, and stable radiation patterns over the operating frequency bands. The proposed prototype can be utilized for WiMAX, C band, X band and Ku band applications.

articleTitle: Polyaniline modified u-bent fiber optic pH sensor for physiological use
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Chemical deposition of polyaniline was done on decladded u-bent optical fiber probe. Polyaniline modified probe was tested for pH sensing from pH 5.8 to 7.7. The proposed pH sensor is able to detect pH change with 0.1 resolutions near physiological pH region.

articleTitle: A compact dual-band open-ended metamaterial antenna for microwave frequency applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article investigates on a compact dual-band open-ended metamaterial antenna for microwave frequency applications. Designed antenna has been incorporated with U-shaped slot, meandered line inductance and a square stub. Since the designed antenna structure has been applied with open-ended boundary condition, so the shunt constituent parameters are significantly responsible for the zeroth order resonance. The designed compact antenna having a total footprint area of 0.266λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.092λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with respect to the zeroth order resonance frequency of 2.58GHz. The designed antenna demonstrates -10dB fractional bandwidth of 4.26% and 28.03% with respect to the center frequency of 2.58 and 5.28GHz respectively. Further, the designed antenna offers an average broadside gain of 1.52dBi and 1.84dBi for both the working bands respectively. In addition to above the designed antenna offers an average radiation efficiency of 76.73% and 95.53% in both the working bands. Design and simulation of the proposed antenna has been performed using HFSS 14.0 3D simulation software and all the results are verified by CST micro Studio 11.0. The performance and size of antenna make it suitable for different WLAN (5.15-5.35, 5.47-5.725, 5.725-5.850GHz) and Wi-MAX (2.5-2.69, 5.2-5.8 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Unified coupled equations for Raman mediated interaction in slow-light regime
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A unified mathematical framework has been presented in this paper to describe various manifestations of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) in the slow-light regime, in presence of multiple pumps while simultaneously considering higher order Stokes. The presented framework also deals with other related optical nonlinearities, and remains valid in the sub-picosecond pulse-width regime.

articleTitle: Hilbert transform based phase extraction algorithm for fringe projection profilometry
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Fringe projection profilometry is one of the most widely used techniques for 3D shape measurement, including digital model generation, system identification, rapid prototyping, object replication, quality control, etc. In order to extract the desired profile information of the test object from the deformed fringe projected interferograms, in this paper, Hilbert transform based fringe analysis technique is utilized. Using analysis based on simulations, the efficiency of the proposed strategy is calculated. The retrieved results are compared with conventional single step as well as multi step phase extraction algorithms. Obtained results conclusively establish Hilbert transform to be optimum as compared to conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Coplanar waveguide fed dual band antenna with square slot and DGS for UWB range
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: An antenna that has a capability to operate in the dual-band of frequency (3.88GHz and 9.99GHz) in the ultra wide band range is presented. A coplanar wave guide (CPW) feeding line and defective ground structure at both the ground layers are the key features of this antenna. The function of the square slot in the radiator element to get dual band resonance in the UWB range. These resonant frequencies can be re-tuned by tuning the dimensions of the slot that make the different operating bands in the designed antenna. A novelty of the designed antenna is able to propagate two channels in the UWB range. The defective ground structure is introduced to improve performance of the antenna at these frequencies.

articleTitle: Comparison of 3D sensing algorithms for single shot fringe projection profilometry
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Phase demodulation algorithms from single fringe pattern have been used widely due to their capability of sensing and measuring dynamic objects. In this paper, the comparison of single shot fringe demodulation algorithms for smooth and complex objects having discontinuities have been demonstrated. Fourier transform (FT) and windowed Fourier transform (WFT) algorithms have been used to extract the 3D phase from the modulated fringe pattern. Since, WFT uses Gaussian filter window at each pixel position to retrieve phase information, hence, it is suitable to extract phase for classifying objects having discontinuities, however due to spectrum leakage at discontinuities, FT causes error and are unable to detect correct phase information for such objects. The merits and demerits of both techniques have been discussed.

articleTitle: Miniaturization and bandwidth enhancement of a dipole antenna using graphene-based RIS
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A reactive impedance surface (RIS) based on graphene circular patch is designed and analytically investigated using transmission line (TL) approach at terahertz (THz) frequency. Surface impedance behavior of the unit cell structure can be tuned by varying the chemical potential assigned in each RIS elements. A dipole antenna, supported by a dielectric material, is mounted over 8×8 RIS structure. It is observed that graphene-based RIS provides a miniaturized resonance along with improved impedance bandwidth and good impedance matching. The proposed structure increases antenna front-to-back ratio (FBr) by 12 dB.

articleTitle: Five points method of calibration for six-port receivers
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new calibration technique for linear six-port based receivers. It is shown that only five arbitrary phase shifters with known phase shift values are required for accurate phase calibration of the receivers. Limitations and advantages of the calibration procedure are highlighted. The technique is experimentally validated with the help of a fabricated six-port receiver and four Schottky based detectors at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of 16-channel CWDM system with EDFA and SOA amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper analyses the performance of 16 CWDM channel ranging from 1271nm to 1591nm with optical amplifier, in which cascaded EDFA between two SOA has been used. Optisystem13.0 software tool has been used for designing and simulation of the proposed configuration. System performance is analyzed at different date rates and at different optical fiber length. Maximun Q factor of 33.91 is achieved for 16 channel each at 5Gbps data rate. However at different fiber length better result is obtain at 60km with maximum Q factor of approx 26 and minimum BER of 1.01e-144. Also Flat gain of 60nm is achieved at higher wavelength for 1491nm-1551nm.

articleTitle: A compact integrated antenna-mixer using microstrip circular patch at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper proposes design of a compact integrated antenna-mixer using a microstrip circular patch resonator at 2.4 GHz. The antenna in the structure is a circular microstrip patch antenna. In the mixer design, the field configurations of TM11 resonant mode of the microstrip circular patch resonator are utilized to achieve good RF-to-IF and LO-to-IF isolation without using an IF filter. The mixer uses Schottky barrier diode for mixing purpose and exhibits minimum isotropic conversion loss of 10.73 dB and greater than 17 dB of LO-to-IF and RF-to-IF isolations for 3 dB RF bandwidth of 100 MHz. The integrated antenna-mixer can be used in low power, low cost short range microwave communications and sensor design.

articleTitle: Non-invasive blood components measurement using optical sensor system interface
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a non-invasive technique to measure glucose, hemoglobin, SpO2 and heart beat using both IR and Red LEDs is presented. The device is made to simultaneously measure the blood components in real time. A comparison with invasive measurements is also shown.

articleTitle: Planar Ultra Wideband (UWB) filtenna using hexagonal shaped structure
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel printed monopole antenna with filtering characteristics for ultra-wideband application is presented. The antenna consists of an elliptical radiating patch and a defected ground structure. An LPF is integrated on the feed line to get a sharp cut off at 10.6 GHz which also results in the improvement of out-of-band performance. The filter-antenna configuration is simple, compact and there is considerable improvement from basic antenna configuration. The fractional bandwidth is 115.7% and the impedance bandwidth is 7.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Improved reflector backed UWB fat monopole antenna for GPR application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Short range radar like ground penetrating radar needs large bandwidth for high resolution and low frequency for better penetration. This puts constraints on the antenna design to have a compact UWB antenna at lower center frequency with unidirectional pattern. This paper emphasizes on the improvement of fractional bandwidth of a stepped reflector backed fat monopole antenna for unidirectional radiation pattern throughout the required bandwidth. The design, simulation and experimental results are included in this paper.

articleTitle: Terabit nyquist superchannel transmission using PM-QPSK subchannels
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper depicts the design of 1 Tb/s superchannel transmission using nine Nyquist-spaced subchannels of symbol rate 27.75 Gbaud polarization multiplexed - Quadrature phase shift keying (PM-QPSK) advance modulation format. Nyquist spaced means spacing between two channels is approximately equal to the symbol rate. Proposed model has enormous potential bandwidth capacity of Terabit, which is efficient to carry high data traffic in the form of vedio streaming, cloud computing etc. Results of proposed model is being validated.

articleTitle: Microwave applicators for hyperthermia treatment of cancer: An overview
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Medical applications of microwaves can be divided into three categories-i) Thermal or non-thermal effects of microwaves utilized for treatment of patients, ii) Permittivity measurement/attenuation measurement at microwave frequencies/microwave tomography utilized for diagnosis of diseases, and iii) Microwave energy and/or method utilized for treatment or diagnosis. Treatment methods based on microwave thermal effects called as Microwave Thermotherapy can be divided into following groups: Diathermy - Use of microwave to heat the tissue upto 41°C (applied in physiotherapy: e.g. in the treatment of rheumatic diseases) Hyperthermia - Use of microwave to heat the tissue in the temperature range 41-45°C (applied in Oncology in the treatment of cancer) Thermoablation/Thermodestruction - Use of microwave to heat the tissue above 45°C (applied in Urology: e.g. in the treatment of Benign Prostatic Hyperplacia (BPH)).

articleTitle: RBF neural network nonlinear equalizer for 100G 16-QAM coherent optical system
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We evaluate the performance of radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) based nonlinear equalizer (NLE) for single carrier (SC) 16-QAM system. We provide the comparison of nonlinearity compensation results of RBFNN-NLE and K - means clustering algorithm in SC 16-QAM system over dispersion managed (DML) and unmanaged links (DUL). The simulation results show that nonlinear penalty reduces by nearly 2 dB and 1 dB for DUL and DML cases respectively.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of CPW low pass filter with good filter selectivity and sharpness factor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, design, implementation, and performance analysis of a low-pass filter (LPF) using coplanar waveguide (CPW) has been carried out in order to obtain good filter selectivity and sharpness factor. Proposed CPW-LPF has been designed and fabricated using the stepped-impedance method. The detail parametric analysis of the filters has been analyzed in terms cut-off frequency, pass-band width, attenuation at resonant frequency, sharpness factor, filter selectivity etc. The fabricated CPW-LPF shows cut-off frequency of 2.5 GHz, with filter selectivity of 22.5 dB/GHz and good sharpness factor of 0.8. The measured performance of the proposed CPW-LPF shows good agreement with its simulated results.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental studies on retro reflection for optical target detection
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: One of the emerging technique nowadays is retro-reflection/cat's eye affect based optical detection and location. The prior detection (before firing) of hidden snipers and various other surveillance devices has been a great challenge. Most military weapon systems has common feature that they have optical or electro-optical sights. One of the techniques can be detection of the retro-reflection from the aiming optical or electro-optical device. In future the retro-reflection based communication with UAVs is also being into consideration. For development of retro-reflection based devices the understanding of the behavior of the retro-reflection from various targets is crucial. In this paper studies have been carried out through simulation and experimentation to study the behavior of retro-reflection for various possible targets.

articleTitle: Effect of surface roughness on bandwidth of a high frequency multiple beam klystron
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Effect of surface roughness on the bandwidth of a high frequency multiple beam klystron (MBK) cavity circuit is investigated. Surface roughness reduces the surface conductivity of the base material which in turn reduces the unloaded quality factor of the cavity and increases the bandwidth of the cavity. First, effective conductivity is calculated analytically for a given surface roughness, and then it is related to the quality factor and 3dB bandwidth of the cavity. Analytical results are compared with those obtained from 3D simulations.

articleTitle: Microwave imaging of subsurface defects in dielectric structures using complementary split ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel microwave subsurface diagnostic procedure for detection of defects inside coated dielectric structures using complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) based planar microwave sensor is presented. The sensor is made to scan the test structure and the shift in resonant frequency at the loaded and unloaded conditions are recorded at each scan point. Quantitative as well as qualitative microwave images of the test region are formed based on these variations. Mathematical model based on the shift in resonant frequency is also developed to retrieve the permittivity distribution of the dielectric test structure. Simulation and experimental results validate the usability of the designed sensor for practical imaging purposes.

articleTitle: Design and performance of rectangular patch heterogenous antenna on for wearable applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a textile antenna is to be designed for wearable applications. The designed antenna has the design parameters of the size is 40 × 35 × 0.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the substrate is Teflon whose dielectric constant is 2.1 and loss tangent as 0.001. The proposed antenna operates at 2.45 GHz. The proposed antenna has a gain of 4 dBi and VSWR is around 1.1 at the resonating frequency. The antenna is used for variety of applications like defence, secvure communication and biomedical applications. The software used for simulation is IE3D simulator.

articleTitle: Analysis of decomposition methods for classification of land-cover targets based on RISAT-1 hybrid SAR images
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The objective of this paper study delineates the m-delta and m-chi space decomposition methods to determine the behaviour of scattering mechanisms in terms of odd bounce, even bounce and volume component for detection of crops and other land cover targets over parts of Burdwan, West Bengal using hybrid SAR images of India's first microwave Radar Imaging Satellite-1 (RISAT-1). It is observed that volume component is similar in both the decompositions. However, this component is over-estimated as compared to odd and even bounce scattering mechanisms for all land cover targets. The supervised maximum likelihood classification has been performed in this paper.

articleTitle: Virtual optical encryption using phase shifted digital holography and RSA algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Optical image encryption is one of the most promising technologies being investigated in the field of data communication, information technology and cloud computing. In this paper, a novel image encryption system based on virtual optical technique, phase shifted digital holography and RSA public key exchange is proposed. In the system, the encryption keys include the wavelength of the laser beam, focal length of the test lens, defocusing distance and scaling factor. The plain text image is encrypted to a cipher by using a phase shifted hologram function. The decryption process involves the phase calculation using phase shifting and sequential line scan algorithms. The keys are exchanged between sender and receiver by using RSA key exchange algorithm. To determine accuracy of the information retrieved by the proposed technique; the mean square error is calculated between the original image and retrieved image.

articleTitle: Ground based bistatic scatterometer measurement of rice crop at C-band in the specular direction
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the bistatic scattering response of rice crop in the specular direction with the azimuthal angle (φ=0) using bistatic scatterometer system at C-band. A rice crop bed of area 4×4 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was prepared at the outdoor field behind the Department of Physics, IIT (BHU), Varanasi for a ground based bistatic scatterometer measurement during different growth stages at co-polarizations (HH and VV) and cross polarization (VH) for the incidence angle 20°-60°. The crop growth variables such as fresh biomass (FBm), vegetation water content (VWC), leaf area index (LAI) and plant height (PH) were also measured at the time of each bistatic scatterometer measurement of the rice crop. The correlation analysis were carried out between the bistatic scattering coefficient and rice crop growth variables at all the incidence angle and polarizations (HH, VV and VH) to select the optimum angle of incidence and polarization for the measurement of rice crop using bistatic scatterometer system at C-band in the specular direction.

articleTitle: Optimal of wavelength converter deployment in WDM optical networks
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Identification and Deployment of Wavelength Converters (WCs) are more important in WDM optical networks. Deployment of WCs at proper location enhances the connection establishment. We have proposed the optimum number of WCs that can be deployed to minimize the blocking of connection with the minimum increase in the network cost. We also find the location for the WCs to be deployed in the network to improve the connection establishment. Simulation results show that connection establishment is improved in proper deployment of WCs in the backbone network.

articleTitle: A wideband plus shaped split dielectric resonator antenna for wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this work, a plus shaped splitted dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is introduced for wideband applications. The designed antenna structure is excited by using a simple co-axial probe feed. The input impedance bandwidth of proposed antenna below -10 dB is 95.7% (3.05 GHz-8.65 GHz) with a center frequency 5.85 GHz. This antenna provides average gain and approximate radiation efficiency of 5.18 dBi and 78% respectively in the working frequency range of 3.05 GHz to 8.65 GHz. Wideband operation is obtained due to the combination of fundamental mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ11</sub> with higher order mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ21</sub> at 3.6 GHz and 6.1 GHz respectively. Parametric analysis was performed to get the optimum values to design proposed antenna. The proposed antenna could be used for Wi-Max and WLAN application.

articleTitle: Microwave reflectometry based technique for detection of hidden crevasses in glacier
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a simple technique is proposed for detection of a hidden crevasse in glaciated terrain. The proposed technique is based on microwave time reflectometry to analyze reflections obtained from the test area. The applicability of the proposed technique is tested in a controlled laboratory environment by demonstrating a setup similar to the glacier terrain. Materials with similar dielectric properties as that of glacier entities such as snow, ice, and air are considered in order to carry out the experiment using the proposed technique. Scanning of the test area is performed using a semi-automated setup to retrieve the 3-D surface plot of the media containing hidden test materials. The results obtained through the proposed experimental setup show that the microwave time reflectometry technique can be used for detecting crevasses in glaciated terrain.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics for microwave photonics
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Characteristics of silicon photonic integrated circuits that have enabled their inclusion in digitial communication systems are discussed. Frequencies and wavelengths of operation of microwave and optical/infrared systems of interest are defined. The uses of optical components in microwave systems are motivated and demonstrations of such microwave optical systems are reviewed. The literature that discusses silicon photonic devices for generation, shaping and processing of microwave signals is overviewed. Microwave photonic applications in which components developed for digital communication can serve as building blocks are discussed.

articleTitle: Synthesis, characterization, and investigation of ambipolar behaviour on FeVO4 nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have successfully synthesized iron vanadate nanoparticles using the ultrasonic path, which exhibits ambipolar character of electrical measurement. FeVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> nanoparticles were formed ~35 nm in after annealing at 600 °C for 120 mins. This method of synthesis of iron vanadate (FeVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) nanoparticles are highly suitable for micro scale-up preparations for memory switching applications. The X-ray diffraction reveals the pure phase of FeVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> nanoparticles and the I-V measurement result shows the ambipolar nature of FeVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> thin film.

articleTitle: Polarization-angle insensitive metamaterial absorber for wide incident angles
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization angle insensitive metamaterial absorber which works for wide incident angles has been proposed for C-band applications. A unit cell of the proposed absorber has an etched Jerusalem Cross (JC) inside a circle at the center of the square patch and four semi circles are rotated around the center circle by 90° each. Absorptivity of the proposed structure at 5.1 GHz is close to 95 % for all the polarization angles under normal incidence. This polarization insensitivity nature is due to the vertically and horizontally symmetric structure of the unit cell. The four semi circles used in the resonator provides incidence angle insensitivity. The angular insensitivity is studied at different radius of four semi circles. When the radius of the semi circles is 3.2 mm, the simulated absorptivity is higher than 90% and the frequency variation is less than 0.95% for incident angles up to 60°.

articleTitle: A plasmonic MIM bandstop filter
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a bandstop wavelength filter designed by incorporating a rectangular groove in plasmonic MIM (Metal-Insulator-Metal) waveguide. The designed bandstop filter is simulated for generating a transmission notch at 1715 nm having a bandwidth of 130nm (from 1650 to 1790 nm). The analysis of the Bandstop filter is done using parametric study.

articleTitle: Study of sequential nanoimprint lithography using optical disc on polymer coated plastic substrate
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article, we present both a facile and cost-effective fabrication based thermal nanoimprint lithography (T-NIL) to prepare sequential 2D nano patterns on a polymer coated plastic substrate. The sequential T-NIL pattern is fabricated using an orthogonal crossing of nanostructure on the linear grating by the help of DVD grating structure which concludes a convenient and cost-effective method in order to fabricate the 2-dimensional sequential patterns. Hence we believe that this proposed technique would add an alternative upon the conventional nano-structure fabrication.

articleTitle: Effect of silver nanoparticle in the upconversion produced by Er3+/Yb3+ codoped TWPO glass
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Effect of the incorporation of silver nanoparticles in the Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>/Yb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> codoped TWPO glass on the frequency UC emission upon excitation at 980 nm has been studied. Two strong green and the red UC emission bands have been observed in the region of the electromagnetic spectrum and assigned by the characteristic transitions of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ion. A large enhancement in the green and red UC emission bands has been reported due to the incorporation of silver nanoparticles in the codoped glass. The prepared glass with silver nanoparticles can be used to develop the upconverting devices.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable ultrashort soliton generation in gas filled kagome hollow core photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The propagation of high power ultrashort pulse in a gas-filled hollow core photonic crystal fiber is analyzed numerically. A wavelength-tunable soliton pulse can be generated by varying the input chirp from 1500 to 600 nm.

articleTitle: A frequency tripler with suppressed harmonics for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A varactor based frequency tripler with suppressed first, second and fourth harmonics of the input signal is presented. Harmonic balance simulations show that the designed tripler delivers an output power of 13.6dBm for an input power of 26dBm at 42 GHz while the first and second harmonics are suppressed by more than 50 dB and the fourth harmonic by 17.5 dB with respect to the output signal at 42 GHz. A 75 pm quartz substrate and GaAs Schottkyvaractor diodes from Rutherford Appleton Laboratory have been used for the circuit design. A metal enclosure has been considered around the microstrip line circuit and the output signal is coupled to a rectangular waveguide using an E-plane probe transition from microstrip line.

articleTitle: Modelling of multicore erbium doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
