abstract: The aim of this paper is to design the MC-EDFA that observed different modes travel through multiple cores at the different wavelengths such as 1550 nm and 1310 nm. Few governing parameters like normalized frequency, effective refractive index for different wavelengths are calculated in order to show the number of modes and patterns of modes traveling through the core. A comparison is done for 1550 nm and 1310 nm wavelengths which portray 1550 nm as advantageous.

articleTitle: Dual-mode dual-band modified slot coupled cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article presents a dielectric resonator based antenna design with dual-mode dual-band characteristics. This article can attract the readers related to antenna community by two different ways: (i) dual mode generation (HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub>) and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</sub>) creates the ability of diversified radiation characteristics; (ii) ability to cover WLAN (5.2 GHz) and WiMAX (2.5 GHz) wireless frequency bands. Parametric Analysis has been done on HFSS simulation software. Optimize results has been verified by using CST-MWS. The proposed design operates in dual frequency bands i.e. 2.55-2.70 GHz and 4.79-5.58 GHz.

articleTitle: A planar dual band circularly polarized antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A dual band circular polarized planar antenna with coplanar waveguide(CPW) feed is presented in this work. A quasi hexagonal stub is used along with an inverted E arm embedded in the ground inorder to produce two circular polarized resonating bands covering bluetooth, mobile satellite services and weather radar surveillance usable bands. The axial ratio bandwidth is further improved by introducing stair shaped modifications in the ground. The presented antenna has been designed and optimized on FR4 substrate of thickness 1.6mm. The simulated result shows that this antenna covers two bands (2.01GHz-2.26GHz) and (2.9GHz-3.1GHz) at VSWR ≤ 2 and AR ≤ 3dB.

articleTitle: A compact triple-band multi-polarized slot antenna for WLAN/WiMAX application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A compact triple-band dual-polarized slot antenna is proposed for WLAN / WiMAX applications. A rectangular slot loop along with inverted L-shaped and C-shaped slots are introduced for achieving triple-band characteristics. By changing the slot-locations, CP behaviour is obtained at the highest operating frequency. The proposed antenna has good impedance bandwidth, compact size (0.248λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.248λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, with λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> being the free-space wave length at 2.4 GHz) and reasonably high gain in the desired operating bands.

articleTitle: First-principle calculations of electronic and elastic properties of LiInTe2 chalcopyrite under different hydrostatic pressures
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Electronic band structure, density of state and lattice constants of LiInTe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> semiconductor have been calculated using first-principle density functional theory (DFT). Elastics stiffness constants, bulk modulus, shear modulus, Poisson's ratio and B/G ratio have been determined under 0 GPa, 2 GPa, 4 GPa, 5 GPa and 6 GPa pressures and found to be stable upto 5 GPa. Computed results are in reasonable agreement with the available results.

articleTitle: Compact dual frequency substrate integrated waveguide semi-ring loop slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel design of dual frequency low-profile substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slot antenna is examine in this article. The proposed antenna design consists of semi-ring loop radiator, square SIW cavity and shorting pin. The semi-ring loop radiating slot etched on broad wall of square SIW cavity to work as dual frequency of operation and shorting pin improve the impedance matching. The proposed antenna slot radiates the electromagnetics wave over the 10 dB impedance band 7.0 GHz-7.14 GHz and 8.76 GHz-8.83 GHz respectively with gain and efficiency are more than 4.89 dB and 96% in impedance bands. The proposed antenna has low profile, high gain, and good radiation efficiency with high FTBR.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic design, fabrication and analysis of carbon veil based radar absorbing composite for aerospace applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper a monolithic radar absorbing composite based on carbon veils (CV) and glass fiber reinforced plastic (GFRP) have been designed and fabricated. The GFRP laminates consist of glass fabrics impregnated with epoxy, whereas optimized weight percentages of carbon fibers have been impregnated with glass fiber in CV using fiber spinning technique. The constituent electromagnetic properties i.e dielectric constant and loss tangent of carbon veil and GFRP laminates have been measured and used in the electromagnetic simulation and optimization of monolithic radar absorbing composite. Further more the optimized configuration have been used for composite fabrication and tested for its electromagnetic absorption. Experimental result shows minimum 10 dB reflection loss (90% electromagnetic absorption) in 8.20-12.40 GHz frequency region. The fabricated composite shows potential application for radar cross section reduction in stealth applications.

articleTitle: Optimal spectral slot width assignment in flexible grid elastic optical network
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In the dynamic flexible grid Elastic optical network, optical frequency spectrum is divided into narrow width slots. Any sequence of slots can be combined to form a channel according to the requirement. In this paper we present the optimum slot width for efficient and effective utilization of spectrum resources with minimum spectral wastage along with the derivation of empirical formula for calculation of blocking probability at various slot width. The carried traffic is simulated on 14 node 21 link NSFNET network.

articleTitle: Routing modulation and spectrum assignment under spectrum conversion in elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The routing modulation and spectrum assignment (RMSA) constraints hinder the performance of elastic optical networks (EONs). To reduce this hindrance, various RMSA heuristics are proposed by utilizing spectrum conversion techniques in a novel way. The key to proposed conversion techniques lies in the selection of a conversion window (CW). To demonstrate the benefits achieved by the proposed heuristics, simulations are performed using scheduled traffic model (STM). To the best of our knowledge this is the first work concerning RMSA under STM using spectrum conversion in EONs. Although the partial spectrum conversion utilizes 17% more spectrum than full spectrum conversion, simulation results highlight the superiority of partial spectrum conversion in terms of the amount of bandwidth accepted and the number of demands accepted in the network.

Author Keywords: routing modulation level and spectrum assignment

articleTitle: Modal characteristics of conventional slot and silicon nanowire optical rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper elucidates the modal distribution of electric field for a vertically wired waveguide on SOI platform. Silicon wires in this paper are of 10 nm diameter and the waveguide is called as silicon nanowire optical rectangular waveguide (SNORW). Pattern of normalized electric field for dominant mode are compared among conventional slot waveguide, ridge slot waveguide and SNORW.

articleTitle: High-order harmonic generation below the ionization potential using laser-ablated Indium plume
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We study high-order harmonic generation from laser ablated Indium plumes below the ionization potential at various driving laser wavelengths. Apart from intense harmonic from the autoionizing state, we also observe enhanced harmonic generation below the ionization potential.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependent crosstalk properties in heterogeneous two core multicore fibers
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Wavelength dependent crosstalk properties in different possible heterogeneous and trench assisted (TA) heterogeneous two core multicore fibers (MCFs) have been analyzed using finite element method (FEM) based FemSIM software and MATLAB, and its performance is compared with that of the homogeneous and TA homogeneous two core MCF. It is observed that with the same core pitch, TA heterogeneous MCFs have lower crosstalk levels and the change in relative crosstalk slope from its parent MCF structure compared to that of the TA homogeneous MCF.

articleTitle: Huygens radiators: A concept for conformal antenna design
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Metamaterial particles are essentially electrically-small radiators with polarization dependency. Previous work on metamaterials was concerned primarily with using such particles to achieve homogeneous media that enabled unconventional propagation. The metamaterial radiators are inefficient if used in isolation, however, if used as an ensemble, they, collectively, radiate efficiently. This suggests their use as antennas. Because of their electrically-small size, metamaterial elements can be considered as Huygens radiators. With this perspective, a systematic procedure for designing directional and efficient antennas can be developed as we demonstrate here. Furthermore, the new perspective and technology can provide conformable antennas for non-planar platforms.

articleTitle: Integrated silicon photonics directional couplers for WDM applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Supermode dispersion characteristics of directional couplers in 250-nm silicon-on-insulator substrate are investigated for silicon photonics WDM applications (λ ∼1550 nm). Experimental results of such a directional coupler based 2×2 wavelength interleavers and 1×4 WDM (δλ ∼ 10 nm) are shown to be consistent with semi-analytical theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: C-band SAR interferometry for change detection analysis in Krishna River Delta
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Delta ecosystem has always captivated the interests of scientists around the world because of its variety of landforms which are subjected to periodic or abrupt changes. The prime objective of this study is to explore the potential of Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) for change detection analysis in Krishna River Delta using C-band Sentinel-1 TOPSAR Interferometric Wide Swath data. The variation in delta dynamics have been analysed on a set of interferometric image pairs acquired from October 2016 to April 2017. An integrated cumulative change map was generated. Profound changes were noticeable in mangrove swamps, vernal pool and agricultural lands. This study has brought out the significance of InSAR for analysing delta dynamics.

articleTitle: A microstrip feeding structure to generate wideband circular polarization in dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents, a microstrip feeding structure to generate wideband circular polarization in dielectric resonator antenna. Wideband circular polarization (CP) has been obtained through the use of modified ground plane and three stubs in the microstrip feed line. The designed CP DRA has shown input impedance bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10 dB) of 70.37% (1.93-4.02 GHz) and axial ratio bandwidth (AR<;3 Db) of 15.28% (2.90-3.38 GHz) in θ = 0°, φ = 0° direction, respectively. It has been observed from CP radiation pattern that the designed antenna shows left-handed CP in θ = 0°, φ = 0° direction. The proposed CP DRA has average radiation efficiency and gain of 89.24% and 1.98 dBic respectively, in broadside direction and it covers entire operating frequency band. The proposed CP DRA is useful for Wi-MAX (3.3-3.6 GHz) and S-band frequency applications. Simulation has been done on HFSS and cross verified with CST-MS software.

articleTitle: Half mode substrate integrated waveguide cavity backed antenna with low cross-polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A new model of half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) cavity backed antenna with low cross-polarization is characterized here. The HMSIW cavity is achieved by intersecting the rotated rectangular substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity across the hypothetical magnetic wall, and transfigure into non-radiating cavity to radiating aperture without applying any radiating slot. Using this technique the size of SIW cavity is reduced 50% over conventional SIW cavity. The proposed antenna is feed by 50Ω GCPW line. Impedance bandwidth of proposed antenna is 2.5% (9.9 GHz-10.15 GHz) over -10 dB reflection coefficient. Gain and radiation efficiency are more than 7.3 dB and 98 % in impedance band. The low cross-polarization level is below 45 dB over co-polarization and high front to backed ratio (FBR), which is more than 25 dB at mid band frequency.

articleTitle: Wideband multi-segment dielectric resonator antenna for MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this article, a two port multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented for wideband applications. The proposed antenna structure consists of three segmented dielectric resonators of same permittivity excited by microstrip line feeding. These feeding structures are oriented in such a way that orthogonal modes are generated in the dielectric resonator. The fractional bandwidth for both port-1 and port-2 is 46.15%. The proposed MIMO antenna achieves a high isolation (S12) of greater than -30dB in the entire operating frequency. This frequency band (5-8GHz) is mainly used for communication satellites.

articleTitle: Design of metalo-dielectric metasurface for field redistribution and image quality improvement for MRI application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We proposed a metal-dielectric composite metasurface which manipulates RF radiation at subwavelength regime to redistribute electromagnetic field such that the magnetic field enhances and electric field diminishes at the center of metasurface. This central part of the metasurface provides the safe region where specimen can be placed unharmed. The enhanced magnetic field is required for image quality improvement. This type of structure has potential to improve the SNR and reduce the scan time of the MRI system.

articleTitle: Structural and optical investigation in holmium doped Y2M0O6 nanophosphors
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The structural and optical characterization of the Ho<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>MoO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> nanophosphors have been performed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy and frequency upconversion (UC) emission studies. The intense green emission has been observed in the developed phosphors under 980 nm diode laser excitation. The UC emission peaks have been observed at green, red and NIR regime. The calculated CIE coordinate (0.31, 0.68) lies in the green colour region which indicates that the developed nanophosphors can be used in green light display devices and near infrared to visible upconverter.

articleTitle: Electrical, optical and photoresponse characteristics of P3HT:PCBM bulk heterojunction device
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Conjugated polymers and their derivatives are of great importance for their applications in electronic and optoelectronic devices. Here, Bulk Heterojunction (BHJ) photovoltaic device having the structure ITO/PEDOT:PSS/P3HT:PCBM/graphene/Al has been fabricated and examined under both dark and illumination conditions. Absorption study confirms the formation of P3HT:PCBM BHJ. Raman spectra show the similar modes for P3HT:PCBM BHJ as pristine P3HT. I-V behavior of the device is found to be very similar to the Schottky behavior under both dark and illumination conditions. Higher change in reverse current as compare to forward current under illumination condition suggests the device exhibit photovoltaic behavior. Double logarithmic J-V characteristics curve shows an overall power law trend, resulting in Ohmic conduction at lower voltage and trap charge limited conduction (TCLC) with the increase in the voltage.

articleTitle: NIR to green light upconversion emission in Er3+ doped CaTiO3 phosphors
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In the current work, the Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> doped CaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> powder samples have been prepared via solid state reaction method. The frequency upconversion (UC) emission spectra and pump power dependence of prepared phosphors was recorded in the range 500 nm to 900 nm wavelength region at room temperature with the help of 980 continuous wave laser diode excitation. The UC emission peaks centered at ~ 524 nm, ~ 545 nm, ~ 661 nm and ~ 800 nm exhibit due to the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11/2</sub> →<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15/2</sub>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>S3/2→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I15/2, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>F9→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I15/2 and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I9/2→<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>I15/2 transitions of the Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ ions respectively. With the help of energy level diagram the UC emission spectra of the optimized sample has been clearly manifested. The colour purity of the developed phosphors has been calculated with the help of Commission Internationale de l'Elcairage (CIE) chromaticity diagram and it is found to be lie in the green colour region. Based on the experimental results the developed phosphors can be efficiently used in NIR to green light upconverter, display devices, etc.

articleTitle: Two-port 3D printed trefoil torus knot antenna with pattern diversity
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A two-port trefoil torus knot antenna with pattern diversity is proposed. The antenna can generate both broadside pattern, and conical beam pattern. Broadside pattern is obtained by exciting a trefoil knot and a conical beam pattern is achieved by exciting a monopole. Both modes are engineered to operate in an overlapped frequency range. The prototype of the antenna structure operating at 2.45 GHz is realized using 3D printing and the performance is measured in an anechoic chamber. The measured overlapping impedance bandwidth (-10 dB) of both patterns is 16.49% from 2.28 GHz to 2.69 GHz with an isolation of 12 dB between two ports. Measured gain at 2.45 GHz is 8.37 dBi and 4.5 dBi for broadside pattern and conical beam pattern respectively. The proposed antenna can be used as pattern diversity ceiling mounted antenna for indoor communications.

articleTitle: Efficiency estimation of all optical contension detection in optical router for 60 Gbps
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, optical logic circuit based on XGM, FWM effect of single SOA symmetry for optical packet contention detection is presented. All the decisions making, and processing of incoming signals are performed in optical domain for data rate of 60 Gbps. The contention detector efficiency is analyzed for increase in input optical power with different pump power.

articleTitle: Resonant behaviour of coupled plasmonic waveguide structure and its application in sensing
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Resonance parameters of coupled plasmonic waveguide resonance (CPWR) structure are investigated theoretically. Substrate dependency help to choose the correct layer parameters for designing a nanoplasmonic sensor. Characterization of waveguide material has been performed along with sensing application.

articleTitle: Tunable single passband microwave photonic filter based on direct generation technique
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: An approach of tunable single passband microwave photonic filter which can be reconfigurable is proposed. Also we demonstrated theoretically that the beating at a photodetector will only generate a dc component, if a phase-modulated signal is applied directly to a photodetector. Through simulation extraordinary flat-top pass band is observed between 2GHz to 19.5GHz center frequency passband values. For center frequency ranging from 6.5GHz to 12.5GHz, almost symmetrical transition from band stop to band pass is observed.

articleTitle: Optical response of dielectric waveguides loaded with compound plasmonic resonators
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In sensing applications of plasmonic nanoantennae, typically, multiple antennae are used (either in a liquid or in periodic arrays), as it is difficult to probe single nanoantenna. We present a numerical study of the optical properties of a dielectric waveguide loaded with a single compound plasmonic nanoantenna and show that a thin nanolayer analyte can be sensed using this structure with a sensitivity of upto 186 nm per RIU. This platform is attractive for performing single-particle sensing, particularly in combination with opto-fluidics.

articleTitle: Guiding of wave with opaque masks
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We discuss a waveguide composed of identical opaque masks such as slits and pinholes. The masks are aligned along a straight line with equal spacing. The eigenmode wave-functions of such waveguide are calculated using perturbation theory in the case of array of slits and are compared with numerical calculations. Such waveguide can be used to guide waves for which transparent material is not available.

articleTitle: Metal assisted slot waveguide biochemical sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Metal and ridge assisted slot waveguide is proposed on the silicon on insulator (SOI) platform for biochemical sensing applications. Slot-based nanophotonic sensors give high sensitivity for detection of bio-analytes and chemicals. The proposed structure is investigated numerically by optimizing the design parameters.

articleTitle: Enhancing microwave properties of epoxy resin at 2.45 GHz using graphite particles for microwave processing application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Microwave heating is the conversion of electromagnetic energy into heat, which basically depends on the dielectric properties of materials being treated. Therefore, the enhancement in dielectric properties of polymer base matrix is necessary for the processing of materials using microwaves. In this work, the dielectric properties of epoxy composites using graphite as filler under various loading (0-30 wt %) are investigated at ~ 2.45 GHz. The dielectric properties of test specimens are measured using the resonant cavity attached to a network analyzer. The results indicate that both dielectric constant and loss factor increase with the increase in loading of graphite particles in the epoxy resin. To validate the actual measurement condition, the S band rectangular cavity operating at 2.45 GHz is simulated in 3D COMSOL electromagnetic module. The improvement of dielectric properties of epoxy using graphite particles indicates that the graphite can be used as susceptor for microwave processing of epoxy based composites.

articleTitle: Evolutionary algorithms for designing metalenses
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper describes an evolutionary algorithm based method for the rapid design of efficient metasurface flat-optics lenses (metalens). Current design methods based on the local-phase approach suffer from reduced efficiency, particularly, towards the edges of the lenses. The shortcomings of the local-phase approach can be addressed by resorting to extended unit-cells. We have recently reported on evolutionary approaches [1] that are helpful in designing such extended unit-cells. The work on beam-deflecting metasurfaces using extended unit-cells reported earlier is extended here to the design of an entire metalens composed of many such beam-deflectors.

articleTitle: Fringe projection profilometry based secured fingerprint sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the application of fringe projection profilometry (FPP) for secured 3D biometric fingerprint recognition system. For the extraction of texture as well as high frequency information in a practical biometric system simple Fourier filtering methods have been used. We also address the issue of 2D photo and video attacks, which implies presenting a photograph or video before authentication system to get un-authorize access. Using the developed spoof detection technique, the recognition system becomes more credible and secure, and can be used for different commercial and non-commercial applications.

articleTitle: Photo response of P3HT: PCBM/SWCNT bulk hetrojunction device
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Here, we report the photoresponse of poly (3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) and 1-(3-methoxycarbonyl) propyl-1-phenyl [6, 6] C61 (PCBM) bulk heterojunction organic devices. Schottky devices having the structure ITO/P3HT: PCBM/Al and ITO/P3HT: PCBM+SWCNT nanocomposites/Al have been fabricated. Prior to the fabrication of devices, Raman & Photoluminescence studies were performed to study the optical characteristics of polymer blend and nanocomposite; these studies confirm the formation of nanocomposite. I-V characteristics of the devices show a remarkable increase in the current upon light illumination. Further, charge transport analysis shows three different voltage dependent charge transport regions.

articleTitle: Laser bio-speckle technique to study bruising caused by height of impacts on Indian Apple using intensity based algorithms
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In the present paper laser bio - speckle technique has been used to study bruising on Indian Apple caused by effect of impacts from different height using intensity based algorithms. Bio-speckle activities have been evaluated using Co-occurrence matrix (COM), Inertia moment (IM) and Absolute value of difference (AVD). Results have been obtained for different heights of impact on apple and compared. It is concluded that higher height of impact will reduce the mean BA of Indian Apple.

articleTitle: On-chip Silicon photonics assisted frequency doubling and pulse generation
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We present a Silicon photonics assisted RF signal processing, in particular, frequency doubling and RF pulse generation. We demonstrate frequency doubling till 10 GHz using silicon PN ring resonator and we present a detailed study on the effect of carrier offset on the power and linewidth of the up-converted RF signal by increasing the Local Oscillator(LO) frequency. We also demonstrate a photonics approach of pulse generation using an on-chip Silicon PN Mach-Zehnder modulator, where RF-signal frequency between 1-12 GHz could be fed and pulsed at various rates from 100-0.1 millisecond.

articleTitle: Design study of a quasi-optical launcher for 2 MW, 170 GHz coaxial cavity gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, design study of a quasi-optical launcher (QOL) for a 2 MW, 170 GHz coaxial cavity gyrotron designed for plasma heating application in the experimental tokamak is presented. The operating mode is chosen as TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34,19</sub>. The launcher is designed for converting the higher order operating mode into a linearly polarized Gaussian like beam. Design parameters of the launcher is numerically optimized through a commercial software Launcher Optimization Tool (LOT). The designed launcher efficiently converts the operating mode into Gaussian like beam with a minimum diffraction loss.

articleTitle: Optoelectronic oscillator: Electron-photon and photon-electron conversion device
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The present work considers the synchronization of a RF signal with the steady-state RF signal existing in the loop. When the fiber delay is small, the governing equations resemble that of a conventional delayed injection locked oscillator. In presence of fiber delay, the shift in beat frequency is observed.

articleTitle: Poly(3, 3”'-dialkylquaterthiophene)/ZnO quantum dots based hybrid p-n junction diode
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The organic-inorganic hybrid p-n junction diode based on poly (3,3"'-dialkylquarterthiophene) (PQT-12) and ZnO quantum dots (QDs) has been fabricated and characterized in this work. The solution process technique is used for the deposition of PQT-12 and ZnO QDs. ITO coated glass is used as substrate and bottom electrode, whereas Ag is used as a top electrode of the vertical hybrid diode. ZnO QDs facilitates the band pass photo-absorption of visible light through PQT-12 film by blocking high energy photons. The diode shows an excellent switching property with the rectification ratio of 3520 under applied bias of ±3 V. The electrical properties of the hybrid diode such as ideality factor and reverse saturation current are calculated as 3.12 and 3.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−s</sup> A, respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of strain-profile and optoelectronic properties of In(Ga)As/GaAs Trilayer QDIP
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Infrared photodetectors with strain-coupled quantum dot structure have better optoelectronic properties compared to the conventional uncoupled structure. In this report, the strain profile and optoelectronic properties have been compared between the strain coupled Trilayer InAs and InGaAs quantum dot infrared photodetectors. The device with InGaAs QDs in its active layer, has longer luminescence peak and better dot formation due to less lattice mismatch between the dot and capping material. Thus, InGaAs based QDIPs would provide better infrared imaging with higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Frequency shifter for photonic multiple microwave frequency measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A new structure for the realisation of multiple frequency measurement by creating a frequency shifter using Photonic principles. The method is based on the shifting of modulated lower sideband of an optical signal until it matches with the original carrier signal frequency and passing through a travelling wave SOA after adding it with the unshifted reference carrier signal followed by a narrowband filter to detect four-wave mixing power above 20 dBm.

articleTitle: Effect of substrate on the performance of metamaterial based absorber
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This study is done to observe the effect of substrate and its thickness on the performance of the metamaterial absorber. Metal-dielectric stack metamaterial structure is designed for alternating layers of silver and silicon dioxide. It is observed that gold provided better absorbance than silicon dioxide. And more the thickness of substrate more absorbance offers by the proposed metamaterial absorber.

articleTitle: Characterising radar cross section signature for evaluation in test range
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Radar Cross Section (RCS) is one of the most important parameter that is essential for tracking as well as evaluating performance of any air-borne vehicle. There are test scenarios where there maybe multiple of such test vehicles. The test engineers face challenges in terms of discriminating the object to track and to interrogate. Therefore, RCS signature characterization is required to be done a priori. This paper focuses on characterizingRCS of air-borne vehicles and analyses the effect of radome shape in RCS signature pattern, which in turn affects the tracking performance in a test range.

articleTitle: Dual segment cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna excited by a novel composite feed
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Comparative simulation study of dual segment cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) with different feed configuration is described in the present investigation. The antenna consists of dielectric ceramic (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 17) as lower segment and Teflon (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.1) as upper segment. The reflection coefficient - frequency characteristics and radiation pattern of the proposed CDRA are investigated through simulation using Ansys HFSS software. The proposed antenna provides simulated input impedance bandwidth of 3.75 GHz over the frequency range 7.77 GHz-11.52 GHz (percentage bandwidth of 38.8 %) with simulated peak gain of 3.54 dB at 8.11 GHz. The antenna provides omni directional radiation patterns in E- and H-planes with fairly low cross-polarization level. Such CDRA can potentially use in radar and satellite communication as a primary feed.

articleTitle: Enhancement of defect induced micro-photoluminescence intensity in Er doped ZnO
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The enhanced micro-photoluminescence (μ-PL) emission property of Er doped ZnO was systematically investigated. The observed μ-PL spectra showed that ZnO microsphere doped with 3 mol% of Er gives the maximum intensity of optical emission.

articleTitle: A compact polarization reconfigurable square slot antenna for WiMAX
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization reconfigurable square slot antenna for WiMAX operation. The proposed antenna comprises a square slot on one side of the substrate and a microstrip feed on the other. Depending on the switching of the pin diode, the antenna exhibits linear polarization at 3.55 and 3.7 GHz and left-hand/right-hand circular polarization at 3.9 GHz. CST simulations are verified by HFSS simulator.

articleTitle: 300 Watt GaN based transmitter for secondary surveillance radar application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A solid state, light weight highly reliable & Compact GaN based 300Watt Transmitter for IFF application is developed interrogator of Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) Applications. Module supports DPSK & PAM modulation which makes it suitable for ICAO Mode S application as well as for Mode 1, 2, 3/A, C. The module generates a fault for High Pulse Width, High VSWR & High Duty Cycle and protects itself by getting OFF. The module has protection against thermal burnt out. This paper gives complete design & measurement results of 300W transmitter.

articleTitle: On-chip four channal multcasting using a coupled cavity system
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We demonstrate an all optical four channel multicasting using Silicon photonic coupled cavity. An aggregate data rate of 7.2Gbps is transmitted. The proposed cavity system breaks the inherent free spectral range and cavity length product relationship. Multicasting is achieved using free carrier dispersion in Silicon induced by a modulated pump which is mapped to four optical channels.

articleTitle: Multi-mode resonator based asymmetric broadband 10dB directional coupler
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A broadband coupler has been constructed using multi-mode resonator (MMR). The resonator primarily resonates in four distinct modes of frequencies. Out of these, three modes are responsible for broadening the operating band. Operating bandwidth may be tuned by the impedance ratio of the proposed resonator. The coupling is tunable by the gap between coupled transmission lines of the coupler. Finally, a forward-wave 10dB directional coupler ranging from 4 to 8 GHz has been designed. The design has advantages like single layer, without bond-wire and compact size.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of solution-processed perovskite photodetector
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The present study reports Perovskite nanoparticles as active layer in solution processed photodetector. Perovskite nanoparticles (CHjNHPbLj) were synthesized by chemical route and their properties were investigated by UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy and field emission scanning electron microscopy measurements. The dark current-voltage characteristics of the device exhibit rectifying behavior. Photoresponse characterization of the device demonstrates responsivity of 0.4 A/W and detectivity of 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> jones at -5V.

articleTitle: Demonstration of indigenous 320 × 256 focal plane arrays: A journey from investigation of varying QD heterostructures and devices, to ultimate demonstration of the thermal imaging sensor array
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Quantum dot based infrared photodetectors has immense application in the field of thermal imaging. In this work, multilayer InAs quantum dot structure capped with GaAs layer were epitaxially grown using solid state molecular beam epitaxial system. The optoelectronic properties of the grown structure suggest higher optical as well as device efficiency and therefore it was used for fabrication of low temperature operating focal plane array. Fabricated 320 × 256 focal plane array exhibited thermal image of a human target at 80 K.

articleTitle: Highly birefringence decagonal photonics crystal fiber with low confinement loss and small effective area
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have proposed a decagonal photonic crystal fiber (DPCF) containing only two types of circular air holes in this paper. It has low confinement loss of 0.01 dB/m, high birefringent nearly 7.85×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and small effective area of the order of few microns at communication wavelength 1.55 μm. This DPCF may be useful in fabricating polarization maintaining devices, telecommunication, non-linear applications and sensor technology.

articleTitle: Subcarrier modulation to improve detuning bandwidth of harmonic mode locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We derive expressions for pulsewidth for an actively mode-locked fiber laser with subcarrier amplitude modulated (AM) RF signal. We show that the detuning bandwidth (also known as locking range) can be increased by modulating the laser cavity loss by subcarrier AM signal instead of the commonly used single tone RF signal. Experiments show a detuning bandwidth of 480 and 820 kHz in a harmonically mode-locked erbium-doped fiber ring laser for modulation index of 0 and 25 % respectively. These values agree well with theory and simulations.

articleTitle: Optical modal analysis in H field using higher order compact (HOC) FDM in combination with Conjugate Gradient method
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: An accurate and explicit semi vectorial magnetic (H) field mode solver is used for a specific rib wave guide based on Fourth Order Compact Finite Difference Method in combination with Conjugate Gradient algorithm. Here optical waveguide modeling is studied by incorporating the effective refractive index concept of the semi conductor rib wave guide structure for simulating the performances of diverse photonic integrated circuits(PICs). Computed normalized indices and modal indices in both H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> and H modes for different materials are observed to be consistent and in excellent agreement with other published results.

articleTitle: Observation of pulse-phase shift in a highly-nonlinear slotted photonic crystal waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A silicon nanocrystal embedded Nonlinear Slotted Photonic Crystal Waveguide (NSPhCW) is proposed to reduce the length of the nonlinear section required in a typical all-optical switching device. Phase-variation of a pulse due to the effect of self-phase modulation and cross-phase modulation has been calculated and analysed under slow-light regime using a modified Nonlinear Schrodinger Equation (NSEs). A 180-degree phase shift is observed in a sub-hundred micrometer length of the NSPhCW even without the effect of XPM. Also, the addition of a control signal increases the change in phase shift more drastically and a same phase shift is attained in a smaller length.

articleTitle: Design of graphene metasurface to mitigate mutual coupling in monopole antenna at lower THz frequency
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a graphene metasurface is developed to reduce mutual coupling between high profile monopole antenna operating at lower THz frequency band. Here, an array of parasite loaded graphene split ring resonator is used to design the metasurface. The metasurface layer is analyzed by the surface impedance model of graphene. By loading the graphene metasurface between the two monopole, 12 dB improvement in the isolation level has been achieved without compromising the antenna performance.

articleTitle: Optical properties of graphene under different hydrostatic pressures
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The optical properties of graphene have been studied using first-principle density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The dielectric function, refractive index and birefringence in parallel and perpendicular polarization of electric field to the plane of graphene under 0 GPa, 5 GPa and 10 GPa pressures have been studied. The values of these parameters at 5 GPa and 10 GPa have been calculated for the first time. In parallel direction, the threshold energy is blue shifted towards the IR region, whereas in perpendicular direction, it is red shifted towards the UV region. The calculated values are in good agreement with the earlier reported values.

articleTitle: Transmission spectrum of a Photonic Crystal ring resonator with different bus configurations: Simulation based observation
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper studies a typical ring resonator in 2D Photonic Crystal with air holes in slab structure that <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">has</sup> been simulated to observe the possible transmission spectrum as shown in the figure. The structures are designed with different bus configurations keeping the ring and all other parameters identical. This helps in the study of the change in transmission characteristics with respect to bus configuration and can likely be improved further to design relevant photonic devices. The algorithm used is Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD).

articleTitle: Asymmetric resonance based nanosensor with enhanced detection efficiency using dual stub coupled plasmonic waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have designed a nanoplasmonic sensor comprising of subwavelength metal-dielectric-metal waveguide coupled to dual nanostubs and quantitatively evaluated the performance of the sensor for refractive index change of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> RIU leading to a figure of merit of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>. Also detailed comparison with recently reported cavity based plasmonic waveguide based sensors have been illustrated which leads to prove the enhanced sensitivity and higher detection efficiency of the proposed nanosensor.

articleTitle: Optical studies in Er3+ doped SrY2O4 upconverting phosphors for display devices
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The chemical co-precipitation technique have been used to synthesize the Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> doped SrY2Ö4 phosphors. The frequency upconversion (UC) emission spectra in the range 400-900 nm were recorded upon the 980 nm radiation. The UC spectra exhibits five distinct bands peaking at ~ 490 nm, ~ 525 nm, ~ 550 nm, ~ 667 nm and ~798 nm owing to the electronic transitions of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> ions. The UC mechanism has been described with the suitable energy level diagram and the pump power dependent study. The Commission International de l'Eclairage (CIE) chromaticity diagram shows that the prepared phosphor is capable of emitting in intense green region and thus can be applied in fabricating display devices.

articleTitle: An image encryption scheme employing quick response codes
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: An asymmetric image encryption scheme combining the concepts of interference, phase-truncation in Fresnel domain, and quick response (QR) code is proposed. The initial scrambling of the input image is carried out using Arnold transformation. The scrambled image is divided into pixel blocks. Each block gets encoded into a QR code that are multiplexed to form a binary matrix. Phase truncation is applied to the binary matrix which gets encoded into two phase-only masks (POMs). During decryption the POMs are combined together to obtain the binary matrix, which is grouped into QR codes and decoded into pixel blocks. The pixel blocks are recombined and descrambling operation retrieves the decrypted image. The scheme is secure and tolerant to noise. Encryption has been carried out digitally, while decryption may be realized using an opto-electronic setup.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling of extrinsic Fabry-Perot Interferometer cavity
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: An optical wave when passed through the mirrors of an extrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer cavity (EFPI) experiences a phase shift in each round trip as a function of the separation between the mirrors are analyzed. Stability as well as the probability of constructive interference in an EFPI is determined using Nyquist stability criterion. The performance when two perfectly parallel surfaces and when there is some tilt between the mirrors in the cavity is also considered with a continuous range of tilt up to which there is possibility of constructive interference.

articleTitle: Wideband circularly polarized CPW fed antenna for bluetooth applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed circularly polarized (CP) antenna for bluetooth (2.4GHz) applications is presented in this paper. The antenna consists of a circular monopole and two semi-circular stubs are attached with ground plane. The antenna shows CP behavior at 2.4GHz with 250MHz axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW). The structure is simulated and studied for the S-parameters and AR values, those suggest its characteristics presented throughout this paper. Radiation patterns are also studied to confirm about the sense of rotation of the electric field which suggests its right handed circular polarization (RHCP) behavior. The antenna is fabricated on FR4 substrate and measured the corresponding values. The simulated and the measured results for the structure were found to be in good agreement with each other, consequently establishing the usability of the component for commercial production and applications.

articleTitle: Sensors for moment of inertia measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This paper explains sensors selection, data acquisition methods, automation procedures for time period measurement in an instrument intended for measuring mass moment of inertia of tactical missiles. Performance evaluation of sensors is also explained in this paper.

articleTitle: Microwave frequency-electromagnetic field 10 GHz radiation exposure impact on rat skin: An oxidative stress insight
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Various systems of military as well as civilian applications are being widely used worldwide, which involve microwave (MW) radiation at X-Band frequency. Besides their innumerable benefits in different areas of commercial and military sectors, increasing scientific evidences have shown that MW exposure may also lead to adverse biological consequence. The present study investigated the effect of 10 GHz MW exposure on skin of experimental rats. The animals were exposed to 10 GHz source in an anechoic chamber for 3 h daily uninterruptedly for 5 consecutive days at constant power density 5.0 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The oxidative stress markers revealed increase levels of free radical generation, lipid peroxidation and advanced oxidation protein products in MW exposed group compared to the sham-exposed group. The antioxidant enzyme SOD was also found to be significantly elevated. Thus, the study showed that 10 GHz MW exposure causes increase in free radical levels and instigated the events of regulation of oxidative stress in rat skin.

articleTitle: Design of ITO based hybrid silicon optical modulator
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, we have investigated the influence of plasmonic material i.e. ITO (Indium Tin Oxide) in a directional coupler based silicon optical modulator. An electric potential of 2V is applied to the device. The characteristics of the optical modulator is observed in the range of 1.31 μm to 1.55 μm wavelength. Also, numerical simulation reveals a coupling length of 2.5 μm. The investigated optical modulator can play a key role in CMOS compatible silicon photonics integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Multiple rhythms in an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This correspondence reports multi rhythmic optoelectronic oscillator. The OEO consists of a driven oscillator in place of the RF filter. Through numerical study it has been shown that depending on different initial conditions the OEO can produce multiple limit cycle oscillations.

articleTitle: Wideband tree shaped SIW antenna for 60GHz applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Tree-shaped substrate Integrated Waveguide antenna is designed for short distance high data rate transformation RADAR applications. The tree shaped antenna is designed by using Rogers RT/Duriod 5880 Substrate and Coplanar waveguide transition is used as a transmission path. This Tree shaped antenna analyzed the characteristic like reflection coefficient, voltage standing wave ratio and electric fields are presented. Tree shaped antenna gives max magnitude of reflection coefficient -53.39dB at 60.1GHz and 1.007 as voltage standing wave ratio at 60GHz. This tree shaped antenna gives 9.96GHz as bandwidth. Dimensions of the tree shaped antenna structure is 5.9*4*0.508mm3. Due to its bandwidth, reflection coefficient, gain and dimensions this tree shaped antenna structure is full fill the requirements of millimeter wave application like wireless LAN and RADAR applications for today's society.

Author Keywords: Grounded Coplanar Wave guide transmission path

articleTitle: A fishing hook shaped dipole antenna for broadband circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A fishing hook shaped dipole antenna is presented in this paper for broadband circular polarization. The dipole antenna is fed through a tapered microstrip line. The circular polarization is generated using the two orthogonal field component having equal magnitude and phase difference of 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. The proposed antenna can be used in general wireless communication services band. The simulated result shows that the proposed antenna exhibit a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 12.60% (4.61 GHz-5.23 GHz) and impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> | <; 10dB) of 30.23% (4.24 GHz-5.75 GHz).

articleTitle: Electrical and optical properties of MEH-PPV: Fullerene (C60) based devices
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Here, we fabricate a polymer: fullerene composite based devices and investigate its electrical and optical responses. Raman spectra and absorption spectra of the composites show no difference in either shape or intensity from spectrum of pristine MEH-PPV suggesting no change in the chemical structure upon incorporation of C60 into MEH-PPV. I-V behavior of the devices found to be very similar to the Schottky behavior. The higher photocurrent of composite based device compare with the pristine device would make this composite a potential candidate for photovoltaic applications.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of tetrakis β-diketonate dysprosium complexes for OLED application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The present work explains the thermal stability of previously reported pure white light emitting dysprosium complexes with acetylacetone (acac) as β-diketonate organic ligand. In the study all the three complexes shows similar curves of TG and DSC for the decomposition of ligand in complexes due to presence of endothermic peak at around 325<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C.

articleTitle: Growth and characterization of GeSn alloys using RF sputtering
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Thin film of GeSn alloy was deposited on the glass and Si-substrates (100) both by physical vapor deposition (RF/DC magnetron sputtering) technique. The morphological, structural, and optical properties of the layers were investigated with transmission spectrum and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). The result shows that the direct bandgap behavior increases in GeSn alloys.

articleTitle: Cost-effective fabrication of Cu2CoSnS4 thin films for photovoltaic applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Here in this report Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (CCTS) thin films were deposited on glass substrate by using sol-gel spin coating technique. From XRD, reveals that peak at 28.6° corresponds to the (112) plane of stannite phase confirming tetragonal structure of CCTS. The FESEM images indicates closely compact, uniform films. The calculated strong optical band gap of the thin films at 1.45 eV can be suitable for photovoltaic applications. The Hall effect measurements revealed the p-type nature of the CCTS thin films.

articleTitle: Effect of InGaAs as a strain reducing layer on molecular beam epitaxy grown InAs quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Theoretical and experimental studies has been presented to understand the impact of InGaAs as a strain reducing layer (SRL) on InAs quantum dots. The ground state photoluminescence peak of InAs quantum dots with varying InGaAs capping layer thickness have been compared with the conventional GaAs capped one. The hydrostatic and biaxial strain distributions of all the samples have also been evaluated. To verify the accuracy of the theoretical work, the simulated data were validated with the experimental data with an average 2.5% error.

articleTitle: High-resolution integrated microwave photonic signal processing
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this talk, I will present an overview of high-resolution processing of analog signals using on-chip stimulated Brillouin scattering. Several functionalities including bandpass filters, bandstop filters, delay lines and phase shifters will be discussed.

articleTitle: Structural, optical and electrical properties of chlorine doped ZnO nanorods for photovoltaic applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Undoped and 10% Cl-doped ZnO nanorod arrays (NRAs) were synthesized by simple, low cost sol-gel hydrothermal method. The XRD pattern confirmed the formation of wurtzite phase of ZnO. Hexagonal structures are clearly observed from the FESEM images. The increment in optical band gap value evaluated from the absorbance spectra was enunciated from the absorbance spectra. The current-voltage characteristic curve clearly indicates an enhancement of nearly 8 times caused due to UV illumination as compared with undoped ZnO NRAs.

articleTitle: Four element composite triangular dielectric resonator antenna for X-Band applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A four element triangular dielectric resonator antenna (TDRA) with each element made of composite material (i.e. combination of two different dielectric materials) is proposed in the present investigation. The simulation study of the proposed design is carried out through Ansys HFSS numerical simulation software. All triangular elements are excited by 50 Ω coaxial probe. The triangular element consists of two sections. The inner section of triangle touching the probe is made of Li<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-1.94MgO-0.02Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> (LMAP) ceramic with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 6.2 while the outer section is made of teflon (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =2.1). The resonating frequency of 10 GHz and percentage bandwidth of 45.53 % for the proposed antenna is obtained within its operating frequency range 8.04-12.78 GHz. Monopole like radiation pattern with low cross polarization levels and peak gain of 4.94 dB obtained for the proposed antenna reflects its potential for X-Band applications. The simulation results obtained for the proposed antenna are also compared with those for single element composite TDRA having same volume as that of proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Effect of longitudinal and shear stress on photonic crystal based ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper analyzes the response of a silicon photonic crystal lattice under longitudinal and shear stresses. With the aid of a ring resonator-based structure, a shift of resonant wavelength from 1.67 μm to 1.56 μm is achieved for a lattice elongation of 0.04 μm. A novel method of characterizing shear strain is considered, leading to an attenuation of 3 dB for a doubling of strain displacement. Such behavior of the lattice can be used for applications involving variable optical attenuators(VOA), accelerometers and similar devices.

articleTitle: U-bend optical fiber pH sensor using multiple sol-gel coating over TiO2
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A wide range and highly sensitive U shaped optical fiber pH sensor utilizing titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) layer with multiple sol-gel coating has been fabricated and demonstrated in this paper. TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer is deposited over uncladded U-shaped fiber to enhance the evanescent field in the pH sensing film. The wide range sensing film is prepared by using three different indicators of various pH ranges. The higher sensitivity of 0.68 dBm/pH was obtained for double layer of sol-gel at 1550 nm with a good linear response. The sensor is also demonstrated for stability, durability and fast response time.

articleTitle: Modeling the physical properties of two-dimensional nanomaterials for optoelectronic applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In our presentation, I will review work done in enabling the development of two-dimensional nanomaterials for optoelectronic applications. The focus will be on the materials and the theories available for modeling them. I will start with a survey of the nanomaterials fabricated and predicted to exist, together with a discussion of their physical properties. This will be followed by a few examples of optoelectronic devices designed using these materials. Finally, we will present an overview of the theoretical tools developed to study electrons and phonons in these materials.

articleTitle: Polarization dependent electro-optic effect in SOI waveguides with laterally diffused P-N junction
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Polarization dependent plasma dispersion effect is investigated for single-mode SOI waveguides (λ ~ 1550 nm) with laterally diffused p-n junction. The lateral p-n junction of desired length is formed initially in 1.5 μm thick SOI layer (BOX-2 μm) by diffusion doping and then the single-mode waveguides with appropriate design parameters (width W, height H, and slab height h) is defined along the junction for simulations studies to estimate V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub> and L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub>. It is observed that the device becomes more and more polarization sensitive as the device layer thickness (H) decreases, which is justified appropriately by calculating polarization dependent confinement factors as well as free carrier overlaps with the corresponding guided modes.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of an unmatched B⊘ifot junction for X-band orthomode transducer applications
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article presents a method of moment (MoM) based analysis of an unmatched BØifot junction for X-band Orthomode transducer applications. For analysis purpose the network has been modelled using cavities and waveguide sections. The analysis has been verified by comparing the obtained frequency response with CST Microwave Studio simulated data. Aperture field distributions at the input and output apertures for port 1 excitation have been plotted to analyze the effect of higher order modes on the field distribution at the apertures.

articleTitle: On contacts to III-nitride deep-UV emitters
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Although contacts to III-nitride visible and UV-A based emitters has been well explored, understanding the contacts to III-nitride deep-UV emitters have attracted research attention recently. Owing to the wide bandgap, both n-type and p-type contact metallization techniques result in a Schottky barrier at the metal-semiconductor interface. A way to reduce the contact resistance is to achieve a higher free carrier concentration in the epitaxial layer. As a result, growth of III-nitride epitaxial layers on native substrates are providing pathways for significant performance improvement. However, understanding the contacts to deep-UV emitters grown on native substrates are necessary to allow further performance improvement.

articleTitle: Bandgap engineered HgCdTe nano-crystal based hetero-junction infrared sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Advantage of remote-sensing in mid wave infrared (MWIR) spectral range (2μm-5μm) due to atmospheric transmission window. Dominant photon detectors in this range are single crystal InSb and HgCdTe, while cost of these detectors is very high and requires cooling around 80K to reduce dark current. Semiconductor Nano-Crystals or Quantum dots (QD) provide an alternative, combining the advantages of speed and Detectivity (D*) of quantum detectors with much reduced fabrication costs compared to single crystal epitaxial materials. This paper highlights synthesis of ternary alloy semiconductor Mercury-Cadmium-Telluride (HgCdTe) colloidal quantum dots and realization of HgCdTe/Si hetero-junction infrared detector sensitive in MWIR range at room temperature. The photo-response of the nano-crystal HgCdTe/Si heterojunction devices is found to have significant response in MWIR region at room temperature.

articleTitle: Estimation of pattern degradation due to mutual coupling and edge effect in finite array
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper a large phased array with more than 1000 elements has been considered for concept validation. Measured mutual coupling of 64 elements in 8×8 configuration is used in method of auxiliary source and finite array scheme. Since mutual coupling of elements alters the excitation of individual radiator in phased scanning array which degrades radiation performance and sometimes become responsible for scan blindness. Mutual coupling data of realized array has been used for estimation which results into 5%-10% degradation in peak SLL. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis methodology to model mutual coupling and array edge effect to estimate degradation in radiation performance.

articleTitle: Width-modulated tapered air-slot based photonic crystal nanocavity
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A width-modulated air-slot photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity is designed and analyzed. A tapered air-slot, instead of a regularly arranged rectangular slot, is used at the center of a W1 PhC waveguide. This is to reduce the vertical radiation loss which occurs at the abrupt termination of a rectangular slot, and also to increase the inline coupling from a waveguide to the cavity. A three dimensional finite difference time domain method is used to calculate the resonant wavelength, quality factor and modal volume of the cavity which are found as 1.559 μm, 3.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> and 0.154 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> respectively.

articleTitle: A compact ultrathin triband metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A novel design of a compact ultrathin wide incidence angle polarization insensitive meta-material based electromagnetic wave absorber is reported here. The unit cell of this absorber consists of two concentric circular ring enclosed by a square ring. Each ring is responsible for one band of absorption. Periodically extending this unit cell structure a two dimensional absorber is achieved. Because of its symmetric structure this absorbs electromagnetic wave with different directions of electric field and for incidence angle -45° to +45°. The unit cell size 1.27×1.27 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and thickness 0.106 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The simulations done using CST and HFSS. Results from both the simulators are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Dual-mode slot coupled ring dielectric resonator antenna with diversified radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The paper explores a dual-band ring dielectric resonator antenna with diversified far-field characteristics. Two important features of this research article are: (i) simplified excitation mechanism creates two radiating modes inside this ring DRA i.e. HEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</sub>(ii) diversified radiation pattern obtains in different frequency bands i.e. broadsided in lower frequency band while end fire in upper one. The proposed radiator has been optimized on Ansoft HFSS EM simulator. Final results have been confirmed by using CST-MWS. The proposed structure works in two different radiating frequency bands and those are: 2.4-2.9 and 4.5-4.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Maxwell's children remove the bottleneck between microwave electronics and lightwave technology
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Communication is considered extremely important for the growth of human civilization, culture and society. It plays a cardinal role in the existence and development of human society.

articleTitle: 127 Gb/s 16QAM signal generation using optical DAC
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a simple and efficient method to generate 127 Gb/s 16QAM using optical DAC and DP-QPSK signal. We report successful transmission of 254 Gb/s DP-16QAM signal (with FEC) over 720 km of standard single mode fiber.

articleTitle: TerraSAR-X based PsInSAR for subsidence mapping of Burgan oil field, Kuwait
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: The prime focus of this study is to find total subsidence in Burgan oil field, Kuwait using PSInSAR technique. Permanent scatter candidates (PSC) were then selected based on amplitude stability index. Total subsidence was found to be varying between -10 and 10 mm per year on the Displacement Map. PsInSAR has been successfully implemented for finding subsidence between 2008 and 2011 in Burgan Oil field.

articleTitle: Assessment of skin fibrosis using Mueller matrix polarimetry
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Of late, Mueller polarimetry has been investigated as an effective technique for analyzing the tissue optical properties, leading to the differentiation of its normal and malignant variations. Depolarization index, a parameter derived from this technique has been observed to be strongly associated with the scattering properties of the tissue. The work carried out in this study aims to investigate the sensitivity of the depolarization index, to changes in subsurface optical scattering present in optical bilayered tissue models, mimicking the conditions of skin fibrosis.

articleTitle: Polymer clad silica fiber for refractive index sensing application
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A core exposed polymer cladded fiber sensor for refractive index (RI) measurement is presented here. The polymer cladding of the multimode silica fiber was removed from a length of 1.5 cm to act as a sensing region. The working principle of the sensor is based on total internal reflection (TIR) phenomenon. The intensity modulation of the transmitted light is measured as a function of liquid refractive index surrounding the sensing region. The sensitivity obtained for the probe is 13.99/RIU. The fabricated sensor is of low cost, easy to fabricate and have high sensitivity which makes it useful in chemical sensing.

articleTitle: Generation of optical frequency comb by cascading of Mach-Zehnder modulator and phase modulator with polarization controller
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Optical Frequency Comb plays the vital role in the implementation of Elastic Optical Network. An optical frequency comb generation (OFC) by cascading of phase modulator (PM) and the Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) with polarization controller has been demonstrated in this paper. Using this proposed technique it was possible to produce a maximum number of comb with high stability, good spectral flatness and narrow linewidth with less complexity. Simulation results shows the tunablity and feasibility of the proposed technique can be achieved.

articleTitle: Use of correlation coefficient based image analysis scheme for improved accuracy in focal length measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel image analysis scheme based on correlation coefficient for the accurate determination of focal position of a lens. The collimated light is incident onto the lens and is back reflected using a plane mirror then after passed through a coarse grating. Because of the Talbot self-imaging phenomenon, self-images of the grating at certain fixed planes, called Talbot planes, are formed. For each position of test lens, self-images formed at the first and second Talbot planes are captured. The correlation coefficient between the pair of images is computed, and is used as a measure to determine accurately the focal position of test lens. The proposed technique does not require the use of phase measuring algorithms or the translation/ rotation stage.

articleTitle: Linearity analysis of a frequency tripled optically generated radio frequency signal
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: Agilent advanced design systems (ADS) software® is employed to model Mach Zehnder intensity modulator (MZM) based radio frequency generation at 6 GHz. Linearity analysis of the system is implemented in ADS and verified experimentally. Third order intercept point (IP3) is found within acceptable limit of 51dBm which matches closely with the experimental obtained value.

articleTitle: Transmission performance of DMT for optical metro access network using chirped fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: We have presented compensation of dispersion induced non-linear distortion for Discrete Multitone modulation based optical transmission link using chirped fiber Bragg grating (CFBG). CFBG shows improved performance for transmission of 56 Gb/s DMT system over a transmission length of 200 Km.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of a non-polar, M-plane III-nitride quantum cascade detector
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: A mid-infrared (IR) quantum cascade detector (QCD) using non-polar, m-plane III-nitride material system has been designed and the effects of temperature on the responsivity and detectivity performance have been analyzed. A resonant tunneling transport design has been presented for the QCD. Carrier transport in the QCD has been modeled by using rate equation approach incorporating most of the important scattering mechanisms responsible for the intersubband carrier transitions in the QCD.

articleTitle: Transmission of polarization division multiplexed 25-Gb/s data at 1.55 μm over 2 km OM1 fiber
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, we have successfully demonstrated error-free transmission of 25 Gb/s data over 2 km legacy OM1 multi-mode fiber (MMF) at 1.55 μm wavelength. The maximum per-channel bit-rate distance product achieved in this experiment is 50Gb/s-km. The performance of the system has been evaluated in terms of extinction ratio (ER), Q-value, estimated bit error rate (BER), and power penalty. The worst-case Extrinsic Ratio (ER) in either of the two polarizations obtained for 25 Gb/s transmission after 2 km of OM1 MMF is equal to 8.6 dB at BER = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>.

articleTitle: A twisted slotted waveguide array antenna with high gain performance
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: This article presents, four tilted slot milled on the single side of broad-wall in a twist slotted waveguide. The presented design consists of a WR-90 waveguide for X-band applications. A twist is provided with 360 degree in the WR-90 waveguide. The depicted twisted waveguide slot array shows return loss bandwidth of 8.12-9.1GHz. The average gain of presented antenna is more than 8.0 dBi in the return loss bandwidth.

articleTitle: Analysis of infinite array of finite feed gap dipole antenna placed over a reflector
publicationTitle: 2018 3rd International Conference on Microwave and Photonics (ICMAP)
abstract: In this paper, a solution of Maxwell's equation in terms of Floquet modal function is presented for a dipole antenna placed over a metallic reflector having finite feed gap. To reduce the analytical complexity, orthogonal Floquet modal functions are used and normalized with respect to the modal power. The current distribution function suggested to address the finite feed gap.
